## restart-trust-follows-stale-checkout-membership.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main 2977e6c9 (not run). Restart with's automatic workspace trust
  (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/sessions.rs` around 2823–2851) treats the session as managed when its live row carries any
  checkout membership (`working_copy.is_some()`), which the supervisor fills from plain membership with no folder
  identity check. A borrower (an ordinary session attached to another session's checkout by canonical path) skips the
  origin's identity recovery on Restart, and the cwd check compares path spelling only. New launches instead go through
  the identity-checked managed-checkout read, which also refuses checkouts with no creation time. So a folder put at the
  checkout's path outside Farhelm can get automatic Codex or Pi trust through Restart with. Scope: Codex and Pi only; a
  trust switch must be on; the replacement happens outside Farhelm. Plain Restart keeps its stored launch per SPEC.md
  ("Plain Restart and plain Replace keep their stored launch"), so that is not part of this finding. The 2026-10-18
  `reused-checkout-path-grants-trust.md` decision states the required behavior: "the managed-checkout membership read
  used for trust counts a recorded checkout only when the folder at its path still matches the recorded identity; a
  replaced or missing folder counts as ordinary." Its fix (#2354) changed only the new-launch read, and
  `no-birth-time-checkout-archives-reclone.md`'s execution notes "Restart with in such a folder still trusts as before
  (follow-up)" with no tracking item. Bucket highest kept (trust boundary), though that earlier assessment noted it
  gives an attacker nothing.
- Decision: recorded as `fix code` without asking, under the 2026-10-19 clearly-settled rule (triage.md, "Preparing each
  item"), on the 2026-10-18 decision quoted above and SPEC.md "Managed checkouts" (a checkout without a creation time
  "does not trust its agent automatically"). The user can revise it.
- Completion criteria: Restart with decides "managed" for automatic trust through the same identity-checked
  managed-checkout read new launches use, for the session's cwd, so a replaced, missing or creation-time-less folder
  counts as ordinary for borrowers and origins alike. A test covers a borrower whose checkout folder was replaced at the
  same path. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a
  changelog fragment); over it, block and bring it back, keeping the 2026-10-18 complexity gate. Remove the feedback
  file and its index entry.
- Execution: change `kqyyqmztkytltoysnxtptskqlyxlonvt`, bookmark
  `plan/restart-with-trust-identity/01-restart-with-identity-check`. Restart with now uses the existing identity-checked
  ownership read; the scripted-peer test covers a borrower's stale membership after folder replacement. The size gate
  held. Draft PR [#2738](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/2738/changes).

## template-retry-installs-unseen-permanent-delete.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main 2977e6c9 (not run), with the pinned Dioxus 0.7.10 sources. After a
  rename's PUT succeeds and the follow-up preferences and list reads fail, Templates keeps showing an enabled plain
  "delete" (Restorable, with the Undo tooltip) beside Retry. Retry causes no re-render, because the dialog reads the
  resource's loading state with `peek` and never subscribes, so the disabled-while-loading button is never drawn. When
  the reload finishes, the next render installs a Permanent handler before the label edit is painted on the next
  animation frame, and a click in that gap permanently deletes a stored template that fails current save rules, with
  neither the advance "delete permanently" warning nor Undo. SPEC.md (Templates): "The label the user saw decides: a
  click on 'delete permanently' never offers undo, and a click on plain 'delete' always does, even if the template list
  changed in between." SPEC.md's 2026-10-10 sub-second allowance keeps "Guards this spec names explicitly". Frequency is
  unmeasured; the gap is about one frame.
- Decision: the user picked "Named guards hold; the target follows the click" (2026-10-26 highest-bucket triage page,
  Q1): a guard the spec names, such as the delete label, holds even for a click that lands between a render and its
  paint.
- Completion criteria: a click on a Delete whose painted label was plain "delete" never deletes permanently without
  Undo, including when a newer render has changed the kind but not yet been painted; the shape (for example painting a
  disabled button while the list reloads, or refusing a click whose kind differs from what was last painted) is
  execution's choice. A test covers the failed-reload, Retry, kind-change sequence. Remove the feedback file and its
  index entry.
- Execution: implemented in change `rmqlvyzqknnoqyltownzxlvwkrokltvu`, bookmark
  `plan/template-delete-guards/01-retry-permanent-label`; draft PR https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/2745/changes.

## named-restart-reporter-failure-keeps-old-resume.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main 2977e6c9 (not run). For a named Restart with of Pi or OMP with hooks
  allowed, the relaunch keeps the old capture A, expecting the reporter to report B. If preparing the reporter extension
  fails (write error, or an existing file with the wrong bytes), the launch logs a warning and continues without it; no
  report arrives, and a later plain Restart resumes A. SPEC.md (conversation capture) clears the old capture when hooks
  are off "since no report can then replace the old capture", but names only that case. The 2026-10-22
  `named-restart-with-keeps-unreported-old-conversation.md` outcome left this variant out of scope. The non-first-class
  harness filter excludes resuming the wrong conversation, so it does not apply.
- Decision: the user picked "Treat it like hooks off" (2026-10-26 highest-bucket triage page, Q5).
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md says the same clearing applies when the conversation reporter a launch needs cannot be
  prepared. The reporter is prepared before the relaunch transaction decides whether to clear the capture, and a failure
  clears it there, reusing the existing clear-and-restore path (a definitive pre-spawn abort restores it). A test makes
  preparation fail and expects plain Restart to say it cannot resume. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: implemented in jj change `qvksznmsyxpqmtxxxzwurxkvwpyyrrou`, bookmark
  `plan/named-restart-reporter-clear/01-clear-on-reporter-failure`; draft PR
  [#2742](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/2742/changes). Named Pi/OMP restart now checks reporter preparation
  before the existing transactional clear decision, keeping definitive-abort restoration. The regression covers healthy
  reporter retention, a mismatched reporter artifact, rollback, successful clearing and a subsequent plain Restart
  refusal. Specification and changelog match; the feedback file and index entry are removed.

## template-delete-lost-reply-loses-undo.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed as a mechanism by code reading on main 2977e6c9 (not run). When an ordinary template Delete
  commits on the helm but its reply is lost (timeout or transport error), Templates shows the raw error, drops the
  snapshot Undo would need, offers no Undo, and does not reload the list, so the template still shows as present until
  the dialog closes. `delete_template` cannot tell transport failures from helm refusals. SPEC.md (Signing in again):
  "In the desktop app, an action the user started is never lost silently: it either completes and reports its outcome,
  or reports that its outcome is unknown." Manual recovery (save the clean editor again, or Duplicate) works until the
  dialog closes. Very rare against a local helm.
- Decision: the user picked "Say the outcome is unknown and refresh" (2026-10-26 highest-bucket triage page, Q2). On the
  page they also set a direction for the whole topic: "The UI and the Helm fundamentally should have an infallible
  connection. If the connection in any way fails then (a) for desktop that means the app crashes, and (b) for browser
  that's a full page reload. We need to stop adding complexity and causing code review feedback on this topic.
  _Logically speaking_, we should treat messages going between helm and UI as going over an infalliable transport." With
  the pick they asked to "record a near term todo to do all the follow-up work - settle the full story on what the
  behavior should be for all cases, audit all existing complexity due lack of this infallibility, remove all such
  existing compliexity etc. make sure the todo item is detailed enough so there is no problem reconstructing what this
  is about." Two questions raised in chat stayed open: whether the desktop app literally crashes or restarts its
  interface from scratch, and whether GUI request deadlines stay as a watchdog or go away.
- Completion criteria: on a transport failure or timeout of a template Delete, Templates says the delete may have
  happened and re-reads the list, so a deleted template shows as gone; no Undo is offered after a lost reply. Helm
  refusals keep today's error. A test loses the reply of a committed delete. The follow-up the user asked for is already
  in TODO.md's "Near term" bucket as "Treat the GUI–helm connection as infallible" (added during triage on their
  request); this outcome does not carry it out. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: implemented in change `pxtuqvtxwrnkynqumxnrwskryzpxlkvu`, bookmark
  `plan/template-delete-guards/03-lost-delete-reply`; draft PR https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/2748/changes.

## installer-terminal-link-overwrites-new-foreign-file.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main 2977e6c9 (not run). The installer's Terminal-command placement
  (`place_link` in `crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/installation/install.rs`) inspects `~/.local/bin/farhelm`, moves a
  foreign file there aside under a visible name, then publishes with an overwriting `rename`, so a file another program
  writes there between the check and the rename (microseconds; longer during the one-time old-layout move, where an old
  copy is hashed by path and then removed) is lost. A file that was already there is kept. SPEC.md keeps foreign files
  at that path through crashes and interruptions and lists "the installer keeping a user's file" among protections the
  accident-guard carve-out never removes; concurrent writers are not named. A no-replace rename (`RENAME_EXCL` through
  rustix) is already used in the same file for the app.

  complexity gate, if this turns out to be non-trivial block the plan."
- Completion criteria: the final placement of the Terminal command never replaces an entry that appeared after the
  installer's check: it uses a no-replace rename and, on a new arrival, keeps that arrival (or refuses with a re-run
  instruction), with a fallback for volumes without the flag. A recorded old-layout copy that is meant to be replaced is
  moved aside and identity-checked rather than removed by path. A test places a file after the check. Complexity gate:
  if this is non-trivial (well beyond the estimated 20–40 lines plus a test), block and bring it back. Remove the
  feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: implemented in change `lroulnvrxztzopvkwunpqrsymzkkkvss`, bookmark
  `plan/installer-link-noreplace/01-terminal-link-noreplace`; draft PR
  [#2739](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/2739/changes).

## older-installer-rebuild-deletes-late-foreign-app.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.

  its handoff floor (0.31.1-dev.0, so every stable up to v0.31.0) to that release's own published, checksummed
  installer. On its rebuild path, which only a fresh install or an approved old-layout app reaches (downgrading a
  current install takes the in-place path), the old script builds the new app, then moves whatever is at the app
  location aside and deletes it without re-checking, so an app placed there during the roughly one second of local
  building is deleted. Checked in v0.27.0 (matching the fixture byte for byte) and v0.31.0. Published scripts cannot
  change; the only code remedy would be refusing the handoff.

  complexity gate, if this turns out to be non-trivial block the plan."
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md (installation) states that installing a release older than the handoff floor runs that
  release's own installer, with the protections it had then, which include no protection against something put at the
  app location while it builds. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: implemented in change `zprxtrxzsmxkxnpmxlpmyuzzsxzuuvnv`, bookmark

## retained-delete-approval-can-kill-new-tab.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main 1ec66971 (not run; delegated checker, re-read by the triage session).
  Delete's live-work guard reads each tab's liveness twice: first it refuses only for a tab that is unreadable at that
  moment (`hosts.untold()`, `service/session_hosts.rs` around 587-607), then after a tmux round trip it counts only tabs
  that are readable and alive (`live_tabs()`, around 639-668). A tab whose terminal goes from running to unreadable
  between the two reads is missed by both, so a Delete whose prompt said nothing was alive passes, and teardown still
  roots and ends that tab's pinned child. The window is milliseconds and needs a tab connection failure, so it is very
  rare; the route is in shipped code and also affects guarded CLI and agent Deletes. SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations"
  (Confirmed 2026-10-01): "a Delete or Replace whose prompt said nothing was alive ... is refused if the agent or any
  terminal tab is running". The 2026-10-10 coinciding-faults paragraph does not apply (one fault plus timing). Bucket
  highest kept: the action ends work beyond what the confirmation said.
- Decision: recorded as `fix code` without asking, under the 2026-10-19 clearly-settled rule (triage.md, "Preparing each
  item"), on the SPEC.md sentence quoted above and the guard's own rule that an unreadable tab means "cannot tell",
  which refuses. The user can revise it.
- Completion criteria: Delete's guard decides from one reading of each tab's liveness (or rechecks "cannot tell" after
  counting), so a tab that is unreadable at any point while the guard runs makes a nothing-alive Delete refuse. A unit
  test flips a tab from running to unreadable between the two reads and expects refusal. Size gate: about 100 lines of
  diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment); over it, block and
  bring it back. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: implemented in change `qrukvuwpmtulpwkoomyvyvzruqtotxwv` on bookmark
  `plan/delete-unreadable-terminals/01-guard-one-liveness-read`;
  [draft PR #3024](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3024/changes).

## colliding-start-cleanup-ends-winning-terminal.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed as a source route on main 1ec66971 (delegated checker; not run). A new terminal's random 40-bit
  socket name is checked for absence but not reserved; when a start does not finish (its first stage is killed, or the
  start deadline passes), cleanup connects to that socket and sends Shutdown to whatever answers, without checking the
  peer's launch tag. If another start for a different session or tab drew the same name and won, cleanup ends that
  terminal and its program gets a hangup. Needs about a 1-in-10^12 collision between overlapping starts plus an
  interruption within milliseconds. SPEC.md's 2026-10-10 coinciding-faults paragraph may cover it but names no
  random-identifier collision.
- Decision: on the 2026-11-04 highest-bucket triage page (Q2, the five astronomically-unlikely items) the user wrote:
  "all of the ones with a very straight forward fix (including that terminal host what-conts-towards-size things) - just
  go ahead and fix them. for each in the list that isn't a straightorward fix, add them to the FILTER.md as a specific
  case we have accepted." Triage judged this one straightforward.
- Completion criteria: cleanup of an unfinished start shuts down the host at that socket only when its launch tag is the
  one this start wrote; anything else (a foreign or unreadable tag) is left alone and reported as possibly remaining. A
  test covers a foreign host answering at the socket. If execution finds it is not straightforward (over about 100 lines
  of diff, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment, or it needs a design choice), do not fix
  it: instead add a FILTER.md entry accepting this specific case, as the decision says. Remove the feedback file and its
  index entry.
- Execution: took the approved fallback in jj change `zwpxwpwwkptputzlszxztvzlqxsmrqkn`, bookmark
  `plan/unlikely-races-nov4/02-start-cleanup-checks-tag`. A tag check through the existing client would first take over
  the foreign host; a non-displacing probe with matching and foreign-host fixtures needs at least about 140 diff lines.
  Added the specific collision-and-interruption filter instead. Draft PR:
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3022/changes.

## async-process-verification-leaves-stale-signal-authority.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: confirmed as a source route on main 1ec66971 (delegated checker; not run). When force-stopping a terminal
  host that did not end through its protocol, Farhelm verifies the process identity on a blocking thread, then awaits
  that result and sends a bare signal by number with no fresh check. If the host exits and its number is reused inside
  that handoff (microseconds in practice), the signal can hit an unrelated process. SPEC_impl.md's short PID-reuse
  acceptance excludes "asynchronous work" in so many words. Not a straightforward fix: moving the signal into the
  blocking closure can send a signal after the caller gave up, unless guarded, and pidfd is Linux-only.
- Decision: on the 2026-11-04 page (Q2) the user said each item in the group without a straightforward fix goes into
  FILTER.md "as a specific case we have accepted" (full quote under `colliding-start-cleanup-ends-winning-terminal.md`).
  Triage judged this one not straightforward, for the reason above.
- Completion criteria: add a FILTER.md filter for this specific case: a process number reused inside Farhelm's internal
  handoff between verifying a terminal host's identity and signalling it, during forced termination. Say it was accepted
  by the maintainer on 2026-11-04. No code or spec change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: completed the accepted-case documentation in jj change `vzpwwzzwoynwplwktroznrqprzmrvslo`, bookmark
  `plan/unlikely-races-nov4/05-filter-handoff-pid-reuse`. Added only the specific internal verification-to-signal
  handoff filter; no code or spec change. Draft PR: https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3033/changes.

## resize-journal-exhaustion-does-not-trigger-checkpoint.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed on main 1ec66971 (delegated checker; not run). A new terminal's recovery buffer charges 64 bytes
  per applied size change against its 32 MiB cap, but neither the checkpoint trigger nor an orderly stop's skip-the-save
  rule counts size changes. On a nearly silent terminal, about 524,288 distinct resizes can push out output no snapshot
  holds; the next supervisor (after a crash or an ordinary update, which skipped the save) rebuilds that terminal
  without it. This contradicts SPEC.md "no viewer can cause a new terminal's gap" and SPEC_impl.md's "keeps its previous
  snapshot and all the output after it". Only Farhelm's copy of the scrollback is lost.
- Decision: on the 2026-11-04 page (Q2) the user named this one for fixing: "including that terminal host
  what-conts-towards-size things" (full quote under `colliding-start-cleanup-ends-winning-terminal.md`).
- Completion criteria: size changes count toward a checkpoint becoming due and toward an orderly stop's decision to save
  (at the host's own per-resize cost), or the skip checks that the host still holds all output since the snapshot.
  SPEC_impl.md's "The skip counts only processed output bytes, not resizes" changes to match, and the "a resize alone is
  not due" test changes with it. If execution finds it is not straightforward (over about 100 lines of diff, not
  counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment, or it needs a design choice), add a FILTER.md entry
  accepting this specific case instead and correct the spec sentences. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: took the approved fallback in jj change `uptspqzqmtsyxyrokqmzolkxlklttlzp`, bookmark
  `plan/unlikely-races-nov4/04-resizes-count-toward-save`. A complete resize-aware saving candidate, including existing
  regressions and truthful code/spec contracts, measured 207 changed lines (140 before final documentation and
  formatting). Added the specific extreme-resize filter and corrected the implementation spec's retention claim and
  output-only accounting caveat. No code change. Draft PR: https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3030/changes.

## critical-mac-commits-omit-media-flush.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: confirmed as a gap on main 1ec66971 (delegated checker, re-checked by the triage session; no power-cut
  experiment). The full-durability helper (`with_full_sync`, `farhelm-supervisor/src/db.rs`) raises only SQLite's
  `synchronous` setting. Nothing sets `PRAGMA fullfsync` or `checkpoint_fullfsync`, which SQLite leaves off by default,
  and the bundled build does not change those defaults. So on macOS the host-identity creation and web-token rotation
  end in a plain `fsync`, which Apple documents as not forcing data through the drive's own cache. The installer already
  uses `F_FULLFSYNC` for this reason (`farhelm-supervisor/src/installation/mod.rs`). Exposure needs a real power cut on
  a Mac without a battery within seconds of one of those two writes.
- Decision: on the 2026-11-04 highest-bucket triage page (Q3b) the user picked "Accept it; say so", with the motivation:
  "this is borderline if it's really worth it to begin with, and vast majority of people are on macbooks with batteries
  etc."
- Completion criteria: SPEC_impl.md, where it lists the fully durable writes (supervisor "Runtime state" and the helm
  store's paragraph), says that on macOS they are durable only up to the drive's cache (no `F_FULLFSYNC`), and why: a
  borderline benefit, since most Macs running Farhelm have batteries. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its
  index entry.
- Execution: implemented in jj change `rtrxnpztnlmvluovonznsqryypqqnvkx`, bookmark
  `plan/durability-revocations/03-mac-flush-caveat`; draft PR https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3028/changes.

  ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment); over it, block and bring it back. Remove the feedback file and its

## stored-wrapper-breaks-new-prompt-literalness.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: confirmed as a mechanism on main 1ec66971 (delegated checker, plus a harmless `printf`-only check by the
  triage session of how Bash parses such a joined line). At launch the stored wrapper words are joined raw and followed
  by the single-quoted agent words, prompt included, and run by Bash. Today's GUI editor and CLI `--wrapper` refuse
  unbalanced quoting and keep each word's spelling, so newly saved wrappers stay balanced. Wrappers saved by 0.30-0.32
  stored de-quoted words and can hold a lone quote mark. With such a wrapper, a prompt without quote marks makes Bash
  refuse the line (nothing runs); a prompt containing an apostrophe rebalances it, and the part of the prompt before the
  apostrophe is parsed as shell. A hand-built protocol request could also store such a wrapper, but whoever can write a
  template's wrapper can already put any shell there, shown on the approval card.
- Decision: on the 2026-11-04 highest-bucket triage page (Q8) the user picked "Discard: only old templates", having said
  "I don't care about pre-change templates".
- Completion criteria: remove the feedback file and its index entry. No code or spec change.
- Execution: discarded in jj change `zlktotoplwonxtqvvrwmzysyvnmvpypp`, bookmark
  `plan/triage-misc-nov4/04-discard-old-wrapper-finding`; removed the feedback file and index entry under the recorded
  decision to leave old templates unchanged. No code or specification change. Draft PR
  [#3039](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3039/changes).

  item"), on SPEC_impl.md "Answers bind to what was drawn": "Every question, confirmation and destructive prompt goes

  The orphan question is not one of the four prompts named there as staying up through their request. The user can
  revise it.

  token and Cancel with `cancel_for`, so a queued answer after Cancel, or for another row's question, does nothing (no

## dead-host-report-anchor-identity-gap.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: mechanisms confirmed individually, complete route unverified (delegated checker on main ebaaf6a7; the
  reviewer's own disposition was unverified after investigation). A terminal host's child already reaped when a
  supervisor adopts the host is anchored by its process number alone (`hosts/terminal.rs` around 880-895, deliberate),
  so a stale report from the session's previous run whose recorded ancestry happens to contain that reused process
  number could be credited to the current run, and a later Restart could resume that conversation. It needs a report
  still pending across a relaunch, a reused process number and an agent that exited before a supervisor restart.
- Decision: covered, removed without asking. SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations", Confirmed 2026-10-10: the cleanup and
  resume rules "do not extend to ... two independent rare faults coinciding (... a lost report and a reused process
  number, and the like). Under those conditions it is accepted ... that a session's recorded conversation is wrong until
  the agent next reports one, so Restart may resume a different conversation of that agent". The same acceptance settled
  the tmux-pane case of this check (`pid-only-anchoring-admit-earlier-launchs-durable-report.md`). The FILTER.md
  process-number filter does not apply (it covers the signal handoff only). The user can revise it.
- Completion criteria: remove the feedback file and its index entry. No code or spec change.
- Execution: complete; the feedback file and its index entry were removed during triage on 2026-11-07.

## agent-settings-save-overwrites-concurrent-editor.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main ebaaf6a7 (delegated checker), with a wider window than the reviewer's
  equal-length example. Credential delivery (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/credential_delivery.rs`, around
  456-493) reads a Tensorlake host's Claude or Codex settings file, merges Farhelm's keys on the helm, creates
  directories and installs the result; the install (`backend.rs` `install_source`, around 991-1125) compares the
  destination only with the new bytes' hash before `mv -f`. Nothing compares the live file with what was read, and the
  per-host lock serializes only Farhelm's own writers. An edit of any length saved in the roughly six SSH round trips
  after the read is silently undone. The reverse also happens: an agent's own read-modify-write straddling the install
  undoes the new token, and since the delivery record then says delivered, nothing repairs it until the next
  replacement. Since the settings-credentials plan, delivery runs at setup, on a connection whose remembered delivery
  differs, and on every credential replacement while the host is connected, so the likeliest concurrent writer is a
  running agent. Unverified: which agent commands write these files, and the window's length. Not covered by the
  2026-10-21 last-write-wins exception (SPEC.md "One GUI at a time"), which names only GUI saves of launch templates and
  number-key bindings. Bucket: high, not highest (one save's few lines, recreatable in a moment under the 2026-10-14
  rule); proposed on the triage page and not contested.
- Decision: the user picked "Refuse to replace a changed file" on the triage page, 2026-11-07, without comment.
  Principle: Farhelm's delivery into an agent settings file never undoes a change saved to that file after Farhelm read
  it.
- Completion criteria: the final replace checks that the destination still matches the bytes that were read (or is still
  absent) and refuses otherwise. On a mismatch, delivery re-reads and merges once; if the file changed again, it falls
  back to the existing amber warning and retries on the next connection, without recording the delivery as done. One
  SPEC_impl.md sentence states the rule beside the delivery description. Tests cover a change between read and replace,
  for an existing file and for an absent one. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting
  this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment; estimated 50-90); over it, block and bring it back. Remove the
  feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: implemented in change `yqxoupsu`, bookmark `plan/agent-settings-compare-replace/01-compare-before-replace`;
  [PR #3173](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3173/changes). The plan's 2026-11-08 Decision raises the approximate
  code/test/doc size gate to 280 lines.

## openssh-floor-percent-path-disables-stable-host-pin.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed in Farhelm's code on main ebaaf6a7 (delegated checker); the OpenSSH half was not re-verified.
  `ssh_config_path_option` and `escape_config_path` (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/ssh.rs`, around 384-393 and 629-633)
  double every `%` for both `IdentityFile` and `UserKnownHostsFile`, and Tensorlake access uses them with
  `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`. On the reviewer's reading of OpenSSH 7.6 sources, versions before 8.4
  percent-expand `IdentityFile` but not `UserKnownHostsFile`, so with a `%` in the helm state path the known-hosts file
  is read and written at a nonexistent doubled path and every connection accepts whatever gateway key it is shown. A `%`
  appears only through `--state-dir`, an `XDG_STATE_HOME` or desktop state-dir value containing one, or a home path
  containing one. SPEC_impl.md sets the 7.6 floor (around 3259) and specifies the doubling (around 6259-6260); they
  conflict on 7.6-8.3. Bucket highest kept: host-key pinning silently off, exposing delivered credentials to an active
  network attacker.
- Decision: the user picked "All eight as listed" for the batch question on the triage page, 2026-11-07. Principle: a
  helm state path containing a character older OpenSSH parsers cannot carry is an unsupported configuration and is
  refused with a clear message, as SPEC.md requires of unsupported configurations.
- Completion criteria: Tensorlake access refuses a helm state path containing `%`, `"` or `\`, with a message naming the
  path, as `${` is refused today; SPEC_impl.md's path-encoding sentence says so; a test covers each character. Size
  gate: about 100 lines of diff (estimated 15), as above; over it, block and bring it back. The same change settles
  `openssh-floor-misparses-managed-known-host-path.md` and may remove both items. Remove the feedback file and its index
  entry.
- Execution: implemented in jj change `qssyuolxkmwuuoynuxlrlwsqmylqrnzy`, bookmark
  `plan/openssh-state-path-refusal/01-refuse-unsafe-state-path`,
  [PR #3168](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3168/changes). Tensorlake host and builder options refuse `%`, `"`
  and `\` in managed paths with the path and relocation advice. The sibling item is closed in the next PR.

## generated-host-name-collision-adopts-unrelated-sandbox.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: partly correct, by code reading on main ebaaf6a7 (delegated checker). Host creation
  (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs` `create_host_sandbox`, around 530-617) looks up the
  generated name and adopts any sandbox found, with no check of the pending-create marker, then prepares it. The
  reviewer's "credentials replaced before the copied-state check" was fixed by #3081 (delivery now follows the
  copied-supervisor refusal), but a rowless same-name sandbox with no Farhelm install still gets this helm's agent
  credentials written into it. Host Delete's name lookup for a row that never sent a create (`tensorlake/hosts.rs`,
  around 157-191) has the same gap. Realistic sources of such a sandbox are a restore from an older copy of helm state,
  or a second helm run from copied state; independent helms collide about 9e-12 per pair of same-slug hosts.
  SPEC_impl.md says host creation "adopts an existing sandbox, including after a lost create response". Not run. Bucket
  highest: credentials delivered into a sandbox the user did not choose.
- Decision: the user picked "Act only on sandboxes this helm asked for" on the triage page, 2026-11-07, with the
  comment: "with hard complexity gate. there alternative is that we simply don't support this. running multiple
  instances on the same state turn is definitely not a supported thing, so us protecting against this is nice, but no
  insane compexity just to get this. lines of code isn't super important so long as it's _SIMPLE_ and not complicated."
  Principle: Farhelm acts on a reserved-name Tensorlake sandbox only when this helm has a durable record of asking for
  it; running several helms from one state is not supported, so this protection is wanted only if it stays simple.
- Completion criteria: host Add adopts a same-name sandbox only when the row records a sandbox ID or an outstanding
  pending-create marker; otherwise it refuses with a message naming the sandbox ("a sandbox named X already exists"),
  leaving it for "Sandboxes not on this helm". Host Delete skips the name lookup for a row that never sent a create.
  SPEC_impl.md's adoption sentence says "only when this row records an outstanding create". Tests cover adoption with a
  marker and refusal without one. Complexity gate (the user's, replacing the usual line-count gate for this item): the
  fix must be simple, a check of records Farhelm already keeps at the points that adopt or delete by name, with no new
  ledger, lock, protocol field or vendor-side metadata. If it is not that simple, drop the code part and instead state
  in SPEC.md that running more than one helm from the same state (including a copy) against one Tensorlake account is
  not supported, and that reserved-name collisions arising from it are accepted. Either way, remove the feedback file
  and its index entry.
- Execution: complete; implemented in change `krvmworpounurvosqwkvnkyrprqpkxvx`, bookmark
  `plan/tensorlake-name-ownership/01-host-adopt-own-record`;
  [draft PR #3188](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3188/changes). Add refuses a name collision without a saved
  sandbox ID or outstanding create, and removing that refused entry makes no sandbox API calls. Recovery with an
  outstanding create and cleanup by a saved ID remain supported. The independent pre-code simplicity review passed; no
  new ownership state is introduced. Ordinary write durability is retained: a legacy row or power loss that loses both
  records requires removing the entry and explicitly handling the leftover.

## short-helm-tag-collision-destroys-other-builder.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: partly correct, by code reading on main ebaaf6a7 (delegated checker). Every build start and recipe
  deletion calls `reconcile_builder` (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/tensorlake/build.rs`, around 1070-1110), which adopts any
  sandbox answering to the builder name `farhelm-build-<tag>-<recipe>` without checking `pending_create_at`;
  `sweep_builder` (around 1253-1300) then terminates it and deletes its snapshots except this helm's recorded ones. With
  a shared tag and recipe name, one helm's build kills another helm's running builder and deletes the snapshot it was
  making, or in a seconds-long window the one it just made. Independent helms share the 4-character tag about 6e-7 per
  pair; helms run from copied state always do. Not run. Bucket high, not highest: what is lost is a Farhelm-built
  snapshot, which Rebuild regenerates (proposed on the page and not contested).
- Decision: decided with `generated-host-name-collision-adopts-unrelated-sandbox.md` on the triage page, 2026-11-07,
  under the same pick and comment (quoted there). The page had explained that a longer tag would not cover copied or
  restored state and would not be simpler.
- Completion criteria: builder reconciliation adopts and sweeps a same-name builder only when the recipe records
  evidence that this helm asked for it (`pending_create_at`, a recorded builder ID, or an interrupted build start);
  otherwise it leaves the sandbox alone and the build fails safely through the existing "did not go away" wait.
  SPEC_impl.md states the same for builders. A test covers a foreign same-name builder left untouched. The same
  simplicity gate and fallback as that entry apply: if not simple, drop the code part and rely on the SPEC.md statement
  that running more than one helm from the same state is not supported. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: complete; implemented in change `rlrnlzxmvwqxpwswqmnpsmqoxwlwurzk`, bookmark
  `plan/tensorlake-name-ownership/03-builder-adopt-own-record`;
  [draft PR #3190](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3190/changes). Reconciliation sweeps a recorded ID and recovers
  by name only for an outstanding pending create. Build starts are not ownership evidence, as the plan expressly
  permits; ordinary write durability is retained. Foreign name occupants and their snapshots survive a fresh build,
  recipe deletion, and cleanup of a different recorded ID. The independent pre-code simplicity review passed; the fix
  adds no ownership state. The specs describe safe refusal and explicit cleanup when the name stays occupied.

## combined-stop-closes-undisplayed-tabs.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 2e42099a (not run). Row, header and bulk Stop send only the
  `refuse_if_tabs_open` and agent-ended booleans, not the tab count the question showed, and the supervisor closes the
  tabs open when it acts. So when Stop's combined question ("stop the agent and close N tabs") is answered in the
  fraction of a second before a tab another Farhelm window just opened reaches the question (normally 0.2-0.5 s, after
  which the question rewords itself), that tab is closed too. SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations" accepts this only for a
  tabs-only prompt: "Accepted: a terminal tab opened between a tabs-only prompt and the click is closed with the others;
  the prompt need not name the exact tabs it showed." The combined case is accepted by the 2026-10-01 Delete decision
  ("a tab opened between the prompt and the click is still closed") and by the landed stop-closes-tabs plan's acceptance
  ("closes every tab, including one opened in between"), which a browser test asserts; most likely a drafting gap in
  SPEC.md. Bucket: `other` (needs a second GUI, which "One GUI at a time" makes best-effort; the tab lost is seconds
  old); moot once decided.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "both fix spec" (2026-11-09 highest-bucket triage page, Q2, shared with
  `approval-grant-outlives-origin-card.md`).
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md's "Accepted" sentence in "Lifecycle operations" covers any destructive prompt that named
  open terminal tabs, alone or together with stopping the agent, not only a tabs-only prompt: a tab opened between that
  prompt and the click is closed with the others, and the prompt need not name the exact tabs it showed. No code change.
  Remove the feedback file and its index entry, and move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: `complete`; SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations" now accepts a tab opened between any prompt that named open tabs
  (alone or together with stopping the agent) and the click. Executed inline at the maintainer's request (spec-only
  outcomes are not planned). jj change `suototzpkxtuyvronxowztwpwvyktrlu`, bookmark `docs/spec-combined-stop-tabs`,
  draft PR [#3285](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3285/changes).

## approval-grant-outlives-origin-card.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: confirmed as a mechanism by reading the code on main 2e42099a (not run), but not a security issue. An
  "Always allow" (or "Always allow on <host> only") answer checks that the requesting connection is live when the answer
  arrives, then waits for the host lock (normally milliseconds) and saves the permission without checking again. If the
  connection drops during that wait, the card disappears and the request is refused, but the permission stays saved.
  What is saved is exactly the permission the user picked on a card that was live when the answer arrived, for exactly
  the install that asked (the write checks the install identity under the lock); the original command never runs, and
  the GUI already says the permission "may still have been turned on". SPEC_impl.md (the `hosts.commands_without_asking`
  paragraph) says Always allow "stores it only if the card's connection is still live" without saying when liveness is
  checked, and already accepts the same outcome when the request expires after the setting is stored. The 2026-10-10
  decision on `always-allow-grant-permission-host-connection-has.md` (now in `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md`) accepted the
  same check-then-lock order for a repointed or replaced host. The landed own-host-sessions-without-asking plan
  prescribes the current order. Bucket: `other`; moot once decided.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "both fix spec" (2026-11-09 highest-bucket triage page, Q2, shared with
  `combined-stop-closes-undisplayed-tabs.md`).
- Completion criteria: SPEC_impl.md says the liveness check for an "Always allow" answer happens when the answer
  arrives: a connection that ends while the answer waits for the host lock can still leave the chosen permission saved
  for that install, with the request refused and the GUI's existing notice saying the permission may have been turned
  on. This applies to every permission a card's "Always allow" saves (session commands, own-host session management, and
  the fleet and browser grants that share the path). No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry, and
  move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: `complete`; SPEC_impl.md "Permission prompts for agent actions" now says the liveness check happens when
  the answer arrives and that a connection ending during the host-lock wait is the already accepted race, for every
  setting a card's "Always allow" stores. Executed inline at the maintainer's request (spec-only outcomes are not
  planned). jj change `qllywwspstlyoxuttxwnwwvyuznktorz`, bookmark `docs/spec-always-allow-liveness`, draft PR
  [#3286](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3286/changes).

## empty-history-queue-bypasses-bounds.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 2e42099a (not run; no browser reproduction). In the browser grid
  terminal (`crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-model.js`), trimming the deferred-history queue lets an empty queued append
  absorb rows that should be trimmed (`entry.offset += excess`) while the real rows behind it stay, so `queuedRows`
  undercounts (possibly negative, which also removes the cap), and the drain then takes the start of history numbering
  from that shifted offset. History rows end up numbered over the live screen's rows. The painter draws history by
  index, while pointer mapping, link lookup and the click check resolve by absolute row number screen-first, so a click
  on a plain URL painted in that scrollback opens the screen row's URL, with no destination display (plain URLs waive it
  because what is shown is what opens). Copying over that range likely takes the screen rows' text too (not traced in
  detail). Empty appends also escape the row cap and the drain's yield. An honest supervisor never sends empty history
  (`grid_output.rs`), but the protocol allows it, so a malicious, compromised or broken host controls the whole trigger.
  SPEC.md's hostile-host acceptance ("Remote input, session defaults, and availability") covers availability only;
  "Local authority and trust between hosts" says Farhelm defends against what an attached host can do. Not clearly
  settled: the link rule states a reason rather than a requirement, and the existing code deliberately keeps empty
  appends because they settle where history starts. Bucket: `highest` by the letter (established route from a named
  threat actor); the harm is a spoofed link, without code execution or exposed secrets.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "fix code, drop empty scrollback messages on arrival" (2026-11-09 highest-bucket
  triage page, Q3).
- Completion criteria: a zero-row history append no longer occupies the deferred queue: once validated, the numbering it
  carries is applied (it still settles where history starts, which is why the code kept it), and it never absorbs
  trimmed rows, counts toward the row cap, or skips the drain's yield. The two existing comments that justify keeping
  empty appends are rewritten to explain the new handling. History numbering stays exact and never overlaps the screen
  after a trim that meets an empty append (and does not leave a gap either). A JS unit test drives a backlog, an empty
  append and more rows than the cap, and checks the queued-row count, the numbering, and that the link under a history
  row is that row's. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff; over it, block and bring it back. Remove the feedback file and
  its index entry, and move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: `complete`; jj change `rxxmsqssywtyqmozspwkwoztspnsrpkt`, bookmark
  `plan/empty-scrollback-messages/01-skip-empty-history`, draft PR
  [#3289](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3289/changes).

## codex-endpoint-change-retains-environment-key.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 2e42099a (not run). When a recipe selects API endpoint for Codex,
  Farhelm selects `model_provider = "farhelm"` and writes its own keys into `[model_providers.farhelm]` while keeping
  every other key in that table (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/agent_endpoints.rs`, `codex()`), so an `env_key`
  (and any `http_headers`/`env_http_headers`) already in that table survives. With the variable exported by the login
  shell, Codex sends that key to the recipe's endpoint instead of the recipe token (upstream precedence established by
  the reviewer from Codex source, not re-checked); with it unset, Codex errors. Needs a custom image, or a hand-edited
  host, with `env_key` inside the table named exactly `farhelm`; Farhelm never writes one. Unchanged by the work landed
  since the 2026-11-07 deferral (#3077, #3081, #3086, #3126, #3173 compare-before-replace delivery, prepared snapshots,
  sandbox sessions); custom image and snapshot bases are still offered. Codex None and Subscription stop selecting
  Farhelm's provider, so a leftover `env_key` is harmless there. Not clearly settled: SPEC.md "Topology" ("Other
  settings remain intact", and "A custom base's existing authentication is preserved and may be inherited by hosts
  created from it; its author is responsible for that content") describes the current behavior.
- Decision: the maintainer, on the 2026-11-09 highest-bucket triage page (Q1, shared with
  `claude-endpoint-change-retains-custom-headers.md`), in their words: "either farhelm is responsible for provisionoing
  credentials, or the image is. I forget if we support both today. But it's either or. If the user asks farhelm to
  provision credentials and they have credentials in the image, the result is undefined. fix SPEC on that point. That
  said, to the extent that we can address this so that the behavior is better, let's fix code with a hard complexity
  gate and SPEC_impl must state this is a best-effort behavior to do better than what SPEC (user visible contract)
  says." Both are supported today, per agent: a recipe's None leaves credentials to the image, while API endpoint and
  Subscription have Farhelm provision them. Answered on the page that this fully resolves both items without new
  settings.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md (recipe agent choices, "Topology") says that for each agent either Farhelm provisions its
  credentials (API endpoint or Subscription) or the base image and host do (None), and that credentials for that agent
  already present in the image or host configuration when Farhelm provisions it give undefined results. SPEC_impl.md
  says Farhelm does better than that contract on a best-effort basis, and what it does: when it provisions Codex through
  API endpoint, it replaces the `farhelm` provider table wholesale with its own coherent definition (dropping `env_key`,
  header settings and any other leftover keys there) while preserving unrelated providers and root settings. Focused
  merge tests cover a preexisting `env_key` and header settings in that table, without changing the test process's
  environment. Hard complexity gate: about 100 lines of diff for this item (code, tests and docs, not counting this
  ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment); over it, or if the fix needs new settings, block and bring it back
  rather than expanding. Remove the feedback file and its index entry, and move this entry to
  `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: change `ntnzwosmntut`, bookmark `plan/endpoint-credential-ownership/01-codex-provider-table`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3290/changes.

## cache-cleanup-leaves-packed-ref-lock.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed on Farhelm's side by reading the code on main 1fd93044 (not run); Git's side rests on the
  reviewer's citations of Git's source and was not re-checked. After each new checkout the supervisor runs a background
  job on the host's repository cache (the ready-checkout spare build, or Git housekeeping with `gc --auto`, both under
  Farhelm's exclusive cache lock; `spare_build.rs`, `launch.rs`). Every cancellation (supervisor stop or update, a
  crash, a spare-setting or checkout-root change, the ten-minute deadline) is an immediate hard kill
  (`service/spare_builder.rs`, `bounded_command.rs`). A kill while Git rewrites the packed branch and tag list leaves
  `packed-refs.lock`; nothing in Farhelm removes Git lock files (`launch.rs` says "no staging or cache repair policy"),
  so once an upstream ref is deleted every later `fetch --prune` in that cache fails and every new checkout of that
  repository on that host fails at the clone stage until manual repair or 30-day eviction (`repo_cache.rs`). A spare
  build's own pruning refresh is a second route. Contradicts SPEC.md ("a failed build leaves no spare, so a later launch
  can clone normally") and SPEC_impl.md ("leave ordinary visible clone available"). Not clearly settled: several fix
  shapes. No coverage.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "(a) Clear leftover Git locks under Farhelm's cache lock" (2026-11-10 high-bucket
  triage page, Q2).
- Completion criteria: before each Git command Farhelm runs in a repository cache, while holding Farhelm's exclusive
  cache lock, Git lock files left in that cache are removed (at least `packed-refs.lock`; the executor decides whether
  to cover Git's other ref and index locks, and says which in a comment that explains why removal is safe: every Farhelm
  Git process in the cache runs under that lock, so any Git lock found then is a leftover). SPEC_impl.md gains a
  sentence on this repair. A test plants a stale `packed-refs.lock` in a cache whose upstream deleted a branch and shows
  the next checkout succeeds. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting
  `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md`, the queue removal or the changelog fragment); over it, block and bring it back. Remove the
  feedback file and its index entry, and move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: change `wvmwlutktpoo`, bookmark `plan/repo-cache-stale-git-locks/01-clear-stale-git-locks`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3296/changes.

## scoped-cleanup-misses-late-tmux.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 1fd93044 (not run). The tmux here is one the user or an agent runs
  inside a session, not Farhelm's own tmux-based terminals. On scoped Linux hosts, stock tmux moves each pane's program
  into its own `tmux-spawn-*.scope`, outside the session's groups; ending the session's groups kills the tmux server,
  and a pane job that ignores hangup survives unless the machine-wide sweep runs. Since 2026-11-09 scoped cleanup checks
  each group once for a running tmux server before any kill (`crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/sweep.rs`,
  `scope.rs`) and keeps the sweep only on a hit. A tmux server started after that check and before the kill (seconds for
  Delete, which checks every group before ending them one by one) is missed, and Stop, Restart, Delete or tab close
  report success while its jobs run on; after Restart they run beside the new agent. Contradicted SPEC.md "Lifecycle
  operations" ("those programs still end with the agent or tab that started the server") and "Ownership during cleanup
  and provisioning". No coverage (`scoped-stop-without-sweep` landed and is the check in question).
- Decision: the maintainer, 2026-11-10 high-bucket triage page, Q1: "if the issue is just that user started tmux
  sessions don't get killed, that's fine. this is essentially the intent the user has when using tmux, and we can call
  it out in the spec." On the follow-up they picked "Say these jobs survive, and remove the check" over keeping it as
  best effort, reversing the 2026-11-09 decision that kept the sweep when a tmux server is running. Decided together
  with `scoped-cleanup-forgets-ended-tmux.md`.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md ("Lifecycle operations" and "Ownership during cleanup and provisioning") and SPEC_impl.md
  say that programs a user-run tmux places outside the session's process groups are not ended by Stop, Restart, Replace,
  Delete or tab close on scoped hosts, as the intent of running them under tmux, and drop the promise and the pre-kill
  tmux check. The pre-kill tmux check and the sweep it keeps are removed from scoped cleanup, with its tests and the e2e
  regression for it removed or inverted to the new rule; scoped cleanup never runs the machine-wide sweep because of
  tmux. Unscoped hosts keep their sweep unchanged. A changelog fragment states the new behavior (`changed`). One change
  executes both items. Size gate: about 100 lines of added code, tests and docs (removed lines do not count); over it,
  block and bring it back. Remove both feedback files and their index entries, and move both entries to
  `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: change `xvpvnvts`, bookmark `plan/user-tmux-jobs-outlive-cleanup/01-drop-tmux-sweep-check`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3297/changes.

## scoped-cleanup-forgets-ended-tmux.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.

  the pane jobs out of the session's group, and Farhelm keeps no record of them. If a user- or agent-started tmux server
  has already exited (`kill-server`, or its last session closing) while a hangup-ignoring pane job lives on, the

## mac-update-gnu-stat-path.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 1fd93044 (not run). Mac inspection only checks that a `stat` exists
  (`provisioning/backend.rs`, unlike its working-`readlink -f` test); artifact inspection then runs the BSD form
  `stat -L -f '%Lp'` through the SSH command's PATH, chosen from `uname -s` alone, and fails on GNU `stat`. Update
  (manual, Update all, automatic), re-running setup on an existing Mac, and uninstall's stop step
  (`provisioning/macos.rs`, `stat -f '%HT'`) fail every time with a cryptic error; Update is also the documented restart
  path after a reboot. Fresh setup works, but the upload's size reports become unusable, so its 60-second stall timeout
  never arms. The trigger needs `gnubin` deliberately ahead of the system tools for non-interactive SSH commands (for
  example in `~/.zshenv`); a stock Homebrew setup in `~/.zprofile` does not trigger it. Contradicts SPEC.md "Supported
  user environments" (an unsupported configuration is refused with a clear message) and the Mac inspection rules either
  way. Remote Macs not yet in a stable release. Not clearly settled: two fix shapes. No coverage.

## cancelled-suspend-can-accept-queued-answer.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: partly correct, by reading the code on main 1fd93044 (not run). In the Hosts panel, the "Suspend
  <host>?" question for a Tensorlake host is a plain signal (`crates/farhelm-ui/src/hosts.rs`, `suspend_question`): its
  Escape, close and Cancel handlers clear it, and its Suspend button calls the lifecycle request without checking that
  the question it was drawn with is still open. A Cancel and a Suspend handled before the next redraw therefore still
  suspend the host (processes freeze until the user clicks Resume; no data loss is established). That consequence is
  accepted by SPEC.md "Maintainer-confirmed decisions" ("A Cancel and a submit of the same dialog that arrive together
  before a redraw may still submit"), so the finding's `high` bucket overstates it; `other` fits what remains. What
  remains contradicts SPEC_impl.md "GUI: Dioxus", "Answers bind to what was drawn": "Every question, confirmation and
  destructive prompt goes through `ConfirmSlot` ... an answer whose token is not the open one does nothing". Host Remove
  in the same file already uses `ConfirmSlot`; host Suspend is not among the four prompts that stay up through their
  request. Double-clicking Suspend is not a route (the page's operation lock refuses the second request). The session
  toolbar's Suspend question has the same gap and is a separate undecided item
  (`sandbox-lifecycle-questions-lack-opening-guards.md`), not in this scope.
- Decision: recorded without asking under the clearly-settled rule (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/triage.md`,
  "Preparing each item"): SPEC_impl.md states the required mechanism in so many words, the code contradicts it, and the
  fix copies host Remove's pattern. The maintainer can revise it.
- Completion criteria: the Hosts-panel Suspend question opens through a `ConfirmSlot`, the render that draws it reads
  the token, Escape, close and Cancel answer with `cancel_for` on that token, and Suspend acts only when `take` with the
  drawn token succeeds; the question does not stay up through the request (it is not one of the four that do). A UI unit
  test in the style of host Remove's shows a Suspend answer carrying a cancelled opening's token does nothing. Size
  gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md`, the queue removal or a
  changelog fragment); over it, block and bring it back. Remove the feedback file and its index entry, and move this
  entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: change `oyszuqoo`, bookmark `plan/hosts-suspend-confirm-slot/01-suspend-confirm-slot`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3299/changes.

## sandbox-ssh-agent-key-ordering-unresolved.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: partly confirmed by reading the code on main 1fd93044 (not run, no ssh connection). Tensorlake connections
  (snapshot builds and host connections) pass `IdentitiesOnly=yes` with Farhelm's registered key and deliberately keep
  the user's ssh config (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/tensorlake/ssh.rs`, `ssh.rs`), and nothing sets `IdentityAgent`.
  OpenSSH moves a config-named `IdentityFile` key that is also loaded in the agent ahead of the remaining file keys even
  with `IdentitiesOnly=yes` (from OpenSSH's key selection, recalled rather than re-read), so a user whose config names a
  personal key for these hosts and loads it in the agent offers that key first; the module comment saying it is
  "offered, but after Farhelm's key" is then wrong. Unverified: whether Tensorlake's gateway refuses the whole login at
  the first unknown key, as Farhelm's code assumes; if it does, builds fail and the host cannot connect, with a hint to
  register a key the user already registered. SPEC.md "Security" already says builds reach the sandbox "with Farhelm's
  own key alone"; SPEC_impl.md names `IdentitiesOnly=yes` as the mechanism. No coverage.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "(a) Stop consulting the ssh-agent for Tensorlake connections" (2026-11-10 high-bucket
  triage page, Q5), without first checking the gateway live.
- Completion criteria: Tensorlake ssh options add `IdentityAgent=none` for builds and host connections, so only
  Farhelm's key file is offered; the module comment is corrected, the option-list test expectations updated, and
  SPEC.md's "Farhelm's own key alone" covers host connections as well as builds, with SPEC_impl.md naming the mechanism.
  The executor confirms, by reading OpenSSH documentation or a local check, that a `ProxyJump` hop's separate ssh still
  uses the user's agent, and says so in the comment. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not
  counting `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md`, the queue removal or the changelog fragment); over it, block and bring it back. Remove
  the feedback file and its index entry, and move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: change `vxpkpvvnqqwlxyppokuznulvzwxlmynu`, bookmark
  `plan/tensorlake-skip-ssh-agent/01-identity-agent-none`, https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3300/changes. The
  plan's 2026-11-10 Decisions narrowed the completion criteria to disabling the gateway's agent use, with configured
  certificates and hardware-token keys as documented exceptions to first-key ordering; no first-or-only guarantee is
  claimed. The comments, specifications and fragment document both exceptions and their possible refusal, and the
  fragment advises leaving those settings out of the configuration applying to Tensorlake hosts. The unsupported OpenSSH
  7.6 hardware-token override is omitted under the agreed fallback.

## sandbox-stop-refresh-weakens-click-guards.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 2e42099a (not run). A sandbox session's row-menu Stop and suspend
  fixes whether to ask, and the operation, at the click (`crates/farhelm-ui/src/sandbox_sessions.rs`, `start`), but its
  `execute` callback recomputes the no-tabs and agent-ended guards from the session of the latest render
  (`session.tabs.is_empty()`, `session.status.has_ended()`); Dioxus `use_callback` replaces its closure on every render.
  A listing refresh landing during the activity check that runs between the click and `execute` can therefore send a
  weakened guard: a tab another window opened meanwhile is closed without a question, and an agent restarted meanwhile
  (by the command line or an agent) is stopped. The finding argued only the tab guard; the ended-agent guard has the
  same cause. The window is one helm HTTP read, so it is narrow. Bucket: not `highest` (realistically `other`); moot
  once decided. The finding's Suspend-versus-Resume sub-claim is not carried: the direction is captured at the click
  (`Operation::requested`, covered by `captured_suspend_and_resume_keep_their_endpoint_after_a_phase_change`), and the
  remaining button-under-cursor race is the sub-second one SPEC.md accepts (line ~4856) and FILTER.md "Races a person
  would have to win inside a sub-second window" matches. Required behavior, SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations": "When the
  session setting skips a prompt, the click authorizes only the state the screen showed, under the same guards ... a
  Stop whose click showed no tabs is refused if any tab is open, and a Stop whose click showed an ended agent is refused
  if the agent is alive again or cannot be confirmed ended". SPEC_impl.md "Answers bind to what was drawn": a control
  "acts on what the render that drew the control showed, never on state it reads when it runs ... nothing is recomputed
  at send time."
- Decision: recorded without asking under the clearly-settled rule (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/triage.md`,
  "Preparing each item"), 2026-11-09 highest-bucket triage. The maintainer can revise it.
- Completion criteria: Stop and suspend captures the no-tabs and agent-ended guards at the click, alongside the existing
  ask decision, and sends those captured values on both the skipped-question and the answered-question paths (click-time
  values can only refuse more, never authorize more). A test shows a refresh between the click and the request does not
  weaken either guard. The undecided queue item `sandbox-lifecycle-questions-lack-opening-guards.md` is in the same
  component but is not part of this outcome. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this
  ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment); over it, block and bring it back. Remove the feedback file and its
  index entry, and move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: implemented in change `utonlsqkwzolmrklsumnxkuyrzzptnyr`, bookmark
  `plan/sandbox-stop-click-guards/01-capture-guards`, [PR #3337](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3337/changes).

## trailing-upgrade-intentionally-ends-old-private-terminals-and-history.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): the retirement the finding describes is
  current behavior. The supervisor that owns the state directory ends the old private tmux server before it reloads
  sessions (service/core.rs, core/old_terminals.rs), sweeps what ran there one agent or tab at a time within a 15 s
  budget, and never gives an old-kind row a terminal again. SPEC.md "Terminal experience", "Old terminals" bullet,
  accepts it in so many words: "A supervisor that finds that tmux server when it starts ends it, and with it everything
  that still ran in an old terminal … one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal's last
  screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed." and "A failure to end the server or to stop what ran
  there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same,
  accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running." SPEC_impl.md "Ending the old
  private tmux server" repeats both, adding "A sweep that runs out of time leaves the rest for the session's Restart or
  Delete: the conversion commits regardless."
- Decision: skipped under the triage rule for behavior already accepted by the specifications (2026-11-18 highest-bucket
  triage); this is accepted behavior, not a completed fix.
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry immediately, without code or spec changes.
- Execution: complete; removed during the 2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage.

## trailing-legacy-tmux-pane-owner-pid-reuse-marker-sweep.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): the window is real. The startup step
  reads each old pane's environment by bare process number after the process-table snapshot, with no start-time recheck
  (core/old_terminals.rs, procs::read_environ), so a number reused in between could make a new terminal-host tab look
  like an old pane and get swept. The window is a synchronous loop with no waits; sweep roots carry (number, start time)
  pairs. SPEC_impl.md "Runtime state": "Process-number reuse inside a short window is accepted, for now. Decided
  2026-10-05." covers reuse between reading a number and checking it, and excludes only carrying a bare number across
  unbounded waits or asynchronous work, which does not happen here. A cheap optional hardening is re-checking the pane's
  start time after reading its environment.
- Decision: skipped under the triage rule for behavior already accepted by the specifications (2026-11-18 highest-bucket
  triage); this is accepted behavior, not a completed fix.
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry immediately, without code or spec changes.
- Execution: complete; removed during the 2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage.

## trailing-old-terminal-survivor-nothing-alive-delete-authority-gap.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): route confirmed. When startup cannot
  reach the old tmux server, or its sweep fails or runs out of budget, an old agent or tab of the session survives
  unlisted; the desktop app shows the session with nothing alive and sends the nothing-alive Delete guard; the
  supervisor's check does not see old-terminal leftovers; teardown sweeps the whole session and kills the survivor. That
  contradicts SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations" ("a Delete or Replace whose prompt said nothing was alive … is refused if
  the agent or any terminal tab is running"), but it fully matches FILTER.md "Upgrades from older releases combined with
  another rare condition": the trigger needs an old-terminal agent or tab carried through the upgrade plus a startup
  connection or cleanup fault, and the whole consequence is lost processes within the affected session, which that
  filter covers; none of its exclusions (broken update, corrupted database, bricked install, security) applies. The next
  supervisor start retries ending the server. Replace's nothing-alive guard has the same gap. Here the survivor is a
  hidden old tab of a session whose agent had moved to a terminal host.
- Decision: skipped under the triage rule for findings matched by a review filter (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage); a
  filter match says nothing about whether the behavior is acceptable in code.
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry immediately, without code or spec changes.
- Execution: complete; removed during the 2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage.

## trailing-legacy-browser-binary-input-reinterpreted-as-grid-json.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading and git history, not run): the route existed only
  in v0.39.0, the one release with grid-only terminals that still served a browser page. A tab loaded from v0.38.0 or
  earlier and left open across the update sent a paste as one binary message, which the v0.39.0 helm relayed as grid
  input and the supervisor decoded as GridInput::Text, turning a literal JSON paste into unbracketed terminal input.
  v0.40.0 removed the browser interface and browser sign-in (#3401, 6ef88c9a4), the old webview desktop app (#3407,
  1eb4e3751) and `farhelm helm run` (#3953, 156f1703f); SPEC.md says Farhelm serves no browser UI and every helm refuses
  a request that carries an Origin (crates/farhelm-helm/src/middleware.rs origin_is_allowed, wrapping the whole router
  including the terminal socket), and an old tab has no credential the helm accepts. The old v0.38/v0.39 lines were
  spot-checked; the old page's mount gates and xterm's bracketed-paste default rest on the reviewers' reading.
- Decision: already fixed (#3401, #3407, #3953); recorded without asking (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage).
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry immediately, without code or spec changes.
- Execution: complete; removed during the 2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage.

  containers or recipe images) runs the agent and installs the recipe's credentials on the new machine. SPEC.md
  "Topology" (confirmed 2026-10-10) accepts it: "Approvals, settings changes and confirmed operations therefore follow
  the entry. One still in flight when the destination changes or a new identity is adopted (an approved stop, restart,
  rename, create or clone, …) may be carried out against the entry's new machine, and Farhelm adds no check of the
  installation identity to prevent that." The environment module docs say the same on purpose. Leftover inconsistency,
  not acted on: SPEC_impl.md says "A launch is also refused if the target host's connection changed while the card
  waited", which holds for ordinary agent launches but not environment cards; SPEC.md governs observable behavior.

  triage); this is accepted behavior, not a completed fix.

## trailing-old-terminal-migration-omits-live-spare-claim-protection-moved-child-removal.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): route confirmed. Startup's spare-claim
  protection treats every old-terminal launch row as not live whether or not retirement stopped it (service/core.rs), so
  a preparation that survived the end of old terminals (a fault or used-up sweep budget) has its spare claim deleted;
  the deletion's check that a folder was not moved runs only after that folder's contents are gone (checkout_trash.rs),
  while the surviving take moves folders into the new checkout without the cache lock (spare_take.rs). Files are lost
  only if a second session started in that unfinished checkout writes into a moved folder during the deletion. It needs
  an update straight from v0.31-v0.33 (spare takes shipped in v0.31, terminal hosts became the default in v0.34) to
  v0.39 or later during preparation, plus the fault and a narrow race. It contradicts SPEC.md "Managed checkouts"
  ("except claims still in a live launch's clone stage") only when the old launch really is alive. FILTER.md "Upgrades
  from older releases combined with another rare condition" fits: carried-over state plus rare conditions, consequence
  lost work within the affected checkout, no exclusion applies. The judgment call that files written by the second
  session inside the affected checkout count as within the affected sessions was put to the maintainer, who accepted it.
- Decision: the user accepted the batch of plain recommendations (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage page, Q7): filtered
  by FILTER.md "Upgrades from older releases combined with another rare condition"; a filter match says nothing about
  whether the behavior is acceptable in code.
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry immediately, without code or spec changes.
- Execution: complete; removed during the 2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage.

  these things. minimize duplication as this ends up in various places oer time." Principle: a GUI save of configuration
  a launch runs or depends on is refused when the value changed since the view read it; convenience bindings stay
  last-write-wins; this is specified once and implemented through one shared mechanism.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md states the rule (which settings are compare-and-set and which are last-write-wins, in
  line with the 2026-10-26 convenience-state decision), and SPEC_impl.md the shared mechanism. A save carries the value
  it was based on, the helm refuses a mismatch, and the window re-reads, through one common representation that later
  settings reuse rather than per-field code; the post-clone command and host folder overrides use it, with tests. Remove
  the feedback file and its index entry in the same change.

  `plan/checkout-settings-stale-save/01-compare-and-set-settings`,

## trailing-old-terminal-migration-unprotected-spare-retained-subtree-removal.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): route confirmed. Startup's spare-claim
  protection treats every old-terminal launch row as not live whether or not retirement stopped it (service/core.rs), so
  a preparation that survived the end of old terminals (a fault or used-up sweep budget) has its spare claim deleted;
  the deletion's check that a folder was not moved runs only after that folder's contents are gone (checkout_trash.rs),
  while the surviving take moves folders into the new checkout without the cache lock (spare_take.rs). Files are lost
  only if a second session started in that unfinished checkout writes into a moved folder during the deletion. It needs
  an update straight from v0.31-v0.33 (spare takes shipped in v0.31, terminal hosts became the default in v0.34) to
  v0.39 or later during preparation, plus the fault and a narrow race. It contradicts SPEC.md "Managed checkouts"
  ("except claims still in a live launch's clone stage") only when the old launch really is alive. FILTER.md "Upgrades
  from older releases combined with another rare condition" fits: carried-over state plus rare conditions, consequence
  lost work within the affected checkout, no exclusion applies. The judgment call that files written by the second
  session inside the affected checkout count as within the affected sessions was put to the maintainer, who accepted it.
- Decision: the user accepted the batch of plain recommendations (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage page, Q7): filtered
  by FILTER.md "Upgrades from older releases combined with another rare condition"; a filter match says nothing about
  whether the behavior is acceptable in code.
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry immediately, without code or spec changes.
- Execution: complete; removed during the 2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage.

  particular upgrade flow and a user not having done the restarts etc doesn't overturn this. These are general
  principles and statements about how the product operates, not a lawyer's contract". Principle: Farhelm's general
  statements about how the product behaves (sessions survive updates and supervisor restarts) describe its ordinary
  operation; a narrow, separately specified exception in one upgrade flow does not make them wrong and is not a reason
  to qualify them everywhere.
