## trailing-natural-detach-unlocks-before-cancelling-unpolled-grid-input.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): confirmed as an ordering regression.
  detach_naturally in crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/connection.rs releases the attachments lock before the old
  attachment (and the input side whose drop cancels its pump) is dropped, while detach_stalled drops it first and the
  version before the reviewed range did too. SPEC_impl.md: "An attachment that ends drops the input its pump had not
  handed to the runtime and stops the pump at once; what the pump handed over is written before anything a replacement
  attachment sends." FILTER.md "A displaced input task resumes inside an in-progress handoff" does not match (it covers
  only an already-polled send). The trigger is not established for shipped clients (it needs the output stream to fail
  while the terminal lives, and there is no await in the gap), so the bucket is other; it would move to highest if a
  shipped producer were shown.
- Decision: recorded as `fix code` under the clearly-settled rule without asking (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage).
- Completion criteria: Natural detach drops the old attachment's input side before releasing the lock, as detach_stalled
  does (about 5 lines, optional test). Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting
  TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md, the queue removal or the changelog fragment); over that, execution blocks and brings the item back
  to the user. Remove the feedback file and its index entry in the same change.
- Execution: change `ukwxmxkssnrqmwutpqzrtvzxkkzozrsv`, bookmark `plan/triage-misc-nov18/01-natural-detach-input-order`,
  [PR #4156](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4156/changes).

## wayland-enter-overtakes-pending-text-paste.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): confirmed for the mechanism. On Wayland
  a paste waits for the asynchronous clipboard read (and only behind earlier pastes), while typed keys are sent at once
  (terminal/attached.rs), so Enter can run a half-typed command before the pasted rest arrives, which then lands at the
  next prompt. macOS reads the clipboard synchronously. Needs a slow clipboard source or a key-injection macro. SPEC.md
  declines to add complexity for slow clipboards. Bucket: high (highest only if a different command running than the one
  composed counts as lost work in itself).
- Decision: settled by the same pick as `header-actions-follow-unseen-session.md` (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage
  page, Q3): spec note for paste order.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md, next to its slow-clipboard rule, states that on Wayland input typed while a paste is
  still being fetched may reach the terminal before the paste. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index
  entry in the same change.
- Execution: change `ulurrwputntkuvrmprxrnsqnxvwurwlo`, bookmark `plan/triage-misc-nov18/04-wayland-paste-order-spec`,
  [PR #4169](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4169/changes).

## sequence-following-enter-does-not-count-as-moving-on.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main bc98e4ec3 (code reading, not run), reviewed by triage: confirmed in source.
  After a Cmd+X quick-launch sequence is launched with Enter, the terminal keeps focus while the launch is pending. The
  moved-on check (crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/focus.rs `note_press`) treats a press as a repeat whenever it is the same
  keystroke on the same focused control as the previous press, with no time limit, so if the first key the user presses
  afterwards is Enter in that terminal (reaching the shell or agent), it does not count as moving on and the finished
  launch still switches to its session and opens the naming dialog. SPEC.md "Opening and closing" exempts only "an
  accidental double-click or repeated Enter on the launcher's own submit"; the code applies it to any control. Bucket:
  high (ordinary but narrow trigger: Enter must be the first key; the app takes the keyboard to a dialog; nothing is
  lost).
- Decision: the user picked "Drop the exemption everywhere" (2026-11-18 GUI UX triage page, QE-2, round 5), after asking
  in their words: "except for esc spamming I don't agree about swalling when the user is the one initiating the irst
  press to make the dialog/whatever go away. if we apply that consistently, then this seems to also go away - for both
  the launcher window AND the sequence case". Principle: when the user's own press dismisses, answers or submits
  something, their next presses are ordinary input; they reach whatever has focus and count as moving on. Only
  Escape-spamming out of menus and dialogs gets the half-second swallow. Auto-repeat of a held key and a lone modifier
  are not new presses and still do not count as moving on.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md "Opening and closing" drops the exemption for "an accidental double-click or repeated
  Enter on the launcher's own submit" (keeping auto-repeat and a lone modifier), and states the principle above with
  `enter-falls-through-after-dismiss-or-approval.md`'s fence change (one paragraph may carry both). The moved-on count
  in the desktop app counts every fresh press and click after the launch's answer, from the launcher window and from a
  quick-launch sequence; the time-unbounded same-key check goes. Tests: a delayed launch where a second Enter on Launch,
  and an Enter in the terminal after a sequence, each leave the user where they are with the "Started" pill. Size gate:
  about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md, the queue removal or the changelog
  fragment); over that, execution blocks and brings the item back to the user. Remove the feedback file and its index
  entry in the same change.
- Execution: change `znqxzsxqkqsypvvtpprtnomqnzlnvwwt`, bookmark
  `plan/gui-ux-enter-and-focus/01-sequence-following-enter-does`,
  [PR #4206](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4206/changes).

## enter-falls-through-after-dismiss-or-approval.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main bc98e4ec3 (code reading, not run), reviewed by triage: confirmed in source.
  After Enter dismisses an empty quick-launch sequence or answers an approval card, focus is (or returns to) the
  terminal, and the user's own held Enter or a second tap reaches the shell or agent. The pill and cards are outside the
  after-close fence, which SPEC.md's focus rules give to dialogs and menus: "After an Enter or Escape closes the last
  open dialog or menu, the same key held or pressed again within half a second goes nowhere". In both routes the surface
  goes away because the user answered it. Bucket: high as filed.
- Decision: the user said the case itself is fine ("(1) is fine", rounds 2-3: the user actually answered, nothing else
  removed the surface) and picked "Keep this case as is, and narrow the fence to Escape" (2026-11-18 GUI UX triage page,
  QE-1, round 5), applying the principle recorded with `sequence-following-enter-does-not-count-as-moving-on.md`:
  outside Escape-spamming, presses after the user's own answer are ordinary input.
- Completion criteria: no change for the sequence pill or approval cards. SPEC.md's after-close fence keeps the
  half-second swallow for Escape only: after an Escape closes the last open dialog or menu, Escape held or pressed again
  within half a second goes nowhere; an Enter after an Enter closed a dialog or menu reaches what has focus like any
  press. The desktop app's focus code (crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/focus.rs closing-press repeat handling) and its tests
  follow. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md, the queue removal
  or the changelog fragment); over that, execution blocks and brings the item back to the user. Remove the feedback file
  and its index entry in the same change.
- Execution: change `wzytxuptuwvsrxnoqrwmlnppqsrosmxy`, bookmark
  `plan/gui-ux-enter-and-focus/02-enter-falls-through-after`,
  [PR #4231](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4231/changes).

## irreversible-confirmation-focus-contract.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main bc98e4ec3 (code reading, not run), reviewed by triage: Two focus rules
  compete for permanent trash deletion. SPEC.md says trash deletion starts on its confirming answer, then that risky
  irreversible actions start on Cancel. The app follows each rule in different places. Bucket: other.
- Decision: the user picked "Confirm-first stays for the named list" (2026-11-18 GUI UX triage page, QG), in their
  words: "the trash cdeletion case is when the user is already in a flow where the intent is completely obvious and
  clear so a confirm makes sense. you're not being prompted for a "whatch out, this might be an unexpected risk" (like
  you are when you try to launch yolo on a box w/o yolo allowed for example)." Principle: Confirm-first applies where
  the user is already in a flow whose intent is plain; Cancel-first is for prompts warning of an unexpected risk.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md's focus rules say which wins: confirmations named in the Confirm-first list (permanent
  trash deletion among them) start on their confirming answer because the user is already in a flow whose intent is
  plain, and the Cancel-first rule is for prompts that warn of an unexpected risk (YOLO on a host that does not allow
  it, for example). No code change (about 2-3 lines). Remove the feedback file and its index entry in the same change.
- Execution: change `kvszvonzwxkxvynpknnlzzxtsllmuvpl`, bookmark
  `plan/gui-ux-enter-and-focus/03-irreversible-confirmation-focus-contract`,

## header-actions-follow-unseen-session.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): confirmed. The open session's header
  (Stop, Restart, Replace, Delete, environment Suspend/Resume) and the interrupted-session card's Replace look up the
  open session and its state when the click is handled (session_pane/header.rs open_key and menu::actionable;
  session_pane/card.rs), while GPUI dispatches the click to the previous frame's handlers. So when the open session
  changes from A to B (the command line deletes A and the window selects B), a click on A's header in that frame acts on
  B, immediately with Skip session confirmations on. The sub-second race filter does not apply (it excludes acting on
  the wrong session). SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations" says the click authorizes only the state the screen showed;
  applying that to the targeted session is a reading, not its words. Bucket: highest.
- Decision: the user picked "Yes for the target and the drop point; spec note for paste order" (2026-11-18
  highest-bucket triage page, Q3), in their words: "But this must not be done in a random ad hoc way for the two places.
  We need to establish a clear pattern that all components can use that have this problem. I don't want this to turn
  into a whack-a-mole. We need to set the standard, spec it, and have an implementation that implements the key
  mechanisms that get reused whenever this problem arises." Principle: a user action in the desktop app acts only on
  what the frame it landed in showed (which session, its state, where a drop landed), and this is one specified standard
  with one reusable mechanism, not per-site fixes.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md (and SPEC_impl.md for the mechanism) state the standard that an action acts on what the
  clicked frame showed: its target and the state its consent or precondition is taken from. The desktop app gets one
  reusable mechanism for capturing what a control drew and acting on that, and the header controls and the card's
  Replace use it. The mechanism is what `session-actions-use-unseen-liveness.md` and
  `trailing-sandbox-stop-rendered-destructive-guards-refresh-before-dispatch.md` (both already `fix code`) are fixed
  with too, so they are planned together rather than as separate ad hoc fixes. Tests show a stale-frame click acting on
  the drawn session or being refused. Expect this to exceed a single small PR; plan it as such. Remove the feedback file
  and its index entry in the same change.
- Execution: change `suuvxrpspvwq`, bookmark `plan/drawn-frame-actions/01-shown-state-standard-and-header`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4176/changes.

## session-actions-use-unseen-liveness.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): confirmed. The desktop app builds a
  lifecycle action's precondition from the session as the store holds it at the click, not as the clicked frame drew it
  (session_list/menu.rs documents "The row as the store holds it now: what any question is drawn from and any
  precondition is taken from"; the skipped Delete sends at once; the launcher reads its warning state at the press).
  GPUI dispatches a click to the previous frame's handlers, so a push landing in that frame can make a nothing-alive
  Delete carry an agent-alive precondition. SPEC.md "Lifecycle operations" (confirmed 2026-10-01): "When the session
  setting skips a prompt, the click authorizes only the state the screen showed, under the same guards. The request
  carries the matching precondition"; the launcher "carries the precondition matching what the launcher showed at the
  click". Bucket stays highest: the route kills a restarted agent without consent.
- Decision: recorded as `fix code` under the clearly-settled rule without asking (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage).
- Completion criteria: Delete, Stop, Restart, Replace and the Restart with / Replace with launcher send the precondition
  matching the state the clicked frame drew, so the supervisor refuses when more is alive than was shown. Uses the
  shared standard and mechanism the user required on 2026-11-18 (Q3; see header-actions-follow-unseen-session.md), not
  an ad hoc per-site fix; the mechanism itself counts against that item, not this gate. Size gate: about 100 lines of
  diff (code, tests and docs, not counting TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md, the queue removal or the changelog fragment); over that,
  execution blocks and brings the item back to the user. Remove the feedback file and its index entry in the same
  change.
- Execution: change `myrpzummtlwl`, bookmark `plan/drawn-frame-actions/02-launcher-consent`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4204/changes.

## wayland-file-drop-uses-entry-position.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main 7a7899dff (code reading, not run): confirmed in GPUI's Wayland backend (the
  vendored `gpui-pre-linux` crate, vendor/gpui-pre-linux/src/linux/wayland/client.rs): while the drag's file list is
  being read, pointer motion is ignored, and when the read finishes the drag position is set to the entry point; a drop
  with no motion since is delivered there, and the terminal accepts a drop anywhere on its pane. So a file dragged in
  over the terminal and released over the sidebar can be uploaded to the session's host. Releasing before the list
  arrives is discarded safely. The sub-second filter does not apply (a local file crosses to a host). Bucket: highest
  (route established in code; narrow trigger).
- Decision: settled by the same pick as `header-actions-follow-unseen-session.md` (2026-11-18 highest-bucket triage
  page, Q3), with the user's instruction that this follow one specified standard and reusable mechanism, not an ad hoc
  fix; see that entry.
- Completion criteria: a drop is delivered where the pointer was when it was released (the latest position recorded
  while the file list was being read), as a new patch layer on the vendored GPUI Linux crate with its patch file
  (vendor/README.md), plus a unit test. Where the standard from `header-actions-follow-unseen-session.md` applies to
  drop delivery, follow it rather than inventing a separate rule. Remove the feedback file and its index entry in the
  same change.
- Execution: change `nyzknxoyrmmo`, bookmark `plan/drawn-frame-actions/04-wayland-drop-release-point`,
  https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4183/changes.

## approval-answer-acknowledged-after-expiry.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: by a delegated checker on main bc98e4ec3 (code reading, not run), reviewed by triage: confirmed. The
  approval waiter can choose Expired while its answer channel is still alive, and the answer handler's ordinary path
  ignores whether the answer was used and replies 204 (`let _ = entry.answer.send(verdict)` in
  crates/farhelm-helm/src/approvals.rs); only Host Add waits for a receipt. The app shows its late-answer notice only on
  410, so the card disappears silently while the agent got "expired", and an Always allow setting may still have been
  saved. SPEC_impl.md: the answer route "returns 410 once the request no longer waits", and "the answer gets 410 and the
  setting stays on, and the GUI's notice says the answer did not take effect". The rare-glitch filter does not apply
  (success reported for an operation that did not take effect). Bucket: other.
- Decision: recorded as `fix code` under the clearly-settled rule without asking (2026-11-18 GUI UX triage).
- Completion criteria: ordinary approval answers use the receipt Host Add already uses, so an answer that lost the race

  diff (code, tests and docs, not counting TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md, the queue removal or the changelog fragment); over that,

## old-suspension-stamp-labels-later-external-pause.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.

  Farhelm's own Resume clears the stored suspension time (crates/farhelm-helm/src/tensorlake/lifecycle.rs), a later
  suspension reuses it (crates/farhelm-helm/src/manager.rs), and the app labels it "Suspended from Farhelm" with the old
  time (crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/environment_ui.rs). So after a Farhelm Suspend, a resume outside Farhelm and a later
  Tensorlake idle suspension, details wrongly say Farhelm suspended it, at the old time. SPEC.md "Topology" (Tensorlake
  hosts): "Its details say since when, and whether Tensorlake suspended it on its own." Bucket: other (diagnostic
  wording).

  of the backend fixes plan on 2026-11-19 so it can be scheduled separately. A correct fix needs more room than that
  plan allowed to handle a new Suspend while Farhelm records that the sandbox ran, and a Retry after an attempt to clear
  the old timestamp failed.
- Completion criteria: the stored Farhelm suspension time is cleared once the host is seen running again, without racing
  a Farhelm Suspend (which holds the connection), so a later suspension is attributed to Tensorlake with its own time;
  with a test. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting TRIAGE_OUTCOMES.md, the queue

## tunnel-reuses-custom-helm-credential-origin.md

- Outcome: `discard` (revised 2026-10-26 from `fix code`; see Decision).
- Assessment: partly confirmed by code reading on main 2977e6c9 (not run). A desktop tunnel binds `127.0.0.1:0` and
  rejects only the remote port number, then opens `http://127.0.0.1:<local port>` in the system browser. A standalone
  helm signed into from that browser keeps its device secret in that origin's localStorage, with no expiry or port
  binding server-side, and stopping the helm revokes nothing. So when a tunnel gets a port a standalone helm once served
  on, the remote page can read the secret. The default 7433 is outside the ephemeral range; ports from `--port 0` or a
  custom port inside that range are affected. Narrower than the file: only a standalone helm accepts the secret, none
  can run on the desktop app's state directory while the tunnel exists, and later use needs local reach, so the strong
  route is the open tab driving a standalone helm later restarted on that port. SPEC.md: "A remote host must not gain
  unauthorized execution or access to secrets on the helm's machine or another host through Farhelm." The 2026-10-22
  `tunnel-can-take-standalone-helm-port.md` outcome fixed only the remote-number collision.
- Decision: the user first picked "Tunnels avoid ports a helm has served on" (2026-10-26 highest-bucket triage page,
  Q4). Superseded the same day while planning it: once planning review showed the fix needs a new durable record of
  served ports (a database table with no downgrade path, or a separate file) and still misses helms run with another
  state directory, the user answered on the planning page: "what, no, this is too much complexity. drop the whole thing,
  discard".
- Completion criteria: remove the feedback file and its index entry; no code or spec change. (The superseded criteria
  were: the standalone helm durably records each port it serves on, and tunnel port allocation skips recorded ports.)
- Execution: change `tmruwznqostqqlpwnwlxpopmrrslkumz`, bookmark `pr/stale-triage-discards`,
  [PR #4367](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4367/changes).

  owner), so the recorded rule makes it a discard; the maintainer asked on 2026-11-21 to discard every decided outcome

  crates/farhelm/tests/spare_builder.rs the test arms `Indirect` only after `await_unrelated_child` returns (lines
  622-623 and 692-693). If the owner dies between spawning its `sleep 300` and publishing that child's PID, the sleep is
  left outside cleanup. The ledger entry the reviewer cites chose the narrower order "wait for PID, arm, then wait for
  readiness", and the reviewer calls full coverage by it ambiguous. The parent cannot own a PID it has not yet been
  told, so closing the gap would need a different mechanism, such as a process group, a subreaper or a parent-death
  signal, and no single obvious shape exists.

  characters and length (`store.rs:1586-1600`). A collision with another host's display name is refused only after the
  Allow, when the write goes through `write_alias_locked` (`hosts.rs:1073-1078` notes that write's "refusals of its own
  (another host's name)"). SPEC.md:2857-2858 accepts this: "On Allow, an edit writes through the same routes as the host
  settings dialog ... with their refusals."

  remaining item that is not likely mooted by the planned infallible GUI–helm connection (TODO.md), is clearly a bug
  needing no spec or product judgment, and is straightforward to fix without complexity or scope creep. The user can
  revise it.
- Completion criteria: narrow the docstring so that only an alias failing the shape rules (control characters, length;
  whitespace-only means none) is refused without a card. It must also say that a collision with another host's name is
  checked by the alias write after the Allow and is refused there with nothing changed. No code change. A test is
  optional; if added, it shows that a colliding alias gets a card and is refused after Allow with nothing written. Size
  gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog

## settings-save-races-final-replacement.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: confirmed by reading the code on main 1fd93044 (not run). When a Tensorlake recipe carries credentials,
  Farhelm merges them into Claude Code's `~/.claude/settings.json` and Codex's `~/.codex/config.toml` on the sandbox at
  setup, on each connection whose recorded delivery is out of date, and when a named token is replaced (SPEC.md
  "Topology"), so some deliveries happen while agents run. Since #3173 the final install compares the destination with
  the bytes read, but the check and `chmod` + `mv -f` are separate steps in one remote command
  (`crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/backend.rs`), so a save by the agent or the user that lands in that gap of a
  few milliseconds (estimated, not measured) is overwritten silently and the delivery recorded as done. Contradicts the
  archived principle "Farhelm's delivery into an agent settings file never undoes a change saved to that file after
  Farhelm read it" (`TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md`, `agent-settings-save-overwrites-concurrent-editor.md`). Fully closing
  it needs a lock the agents also honor; none is known. No coverage.
- Decision: the maintainer asked why delivery edits these files after agents start, then whether credentials could move
  out of the agents' settings files; the page answered that Claude's API endpoint and Subscription and Codex's API
  endpoint could go into the launch environment (Codex's provider through `-c` overrides and an `env_key` token), Codex
  Subscription cannot (Codex owns `auth.json`), and that this is a redesign. They picked "Accept the gap in the spec,
  and add a TODO for launch-environment credentials" (2026-11-10 high-bucket triage page, Q4), and said in conversation:
  "the todo item for credentials hsould be in near term bucket".
- Completion criteria: SPEC_impl.md "Adding Tensorlake hosts" states that a save landing between the final comparison
  and the replacement can still be overwritten, because closing it needs a lock the agents would also honor; the
  archived principle is narrowed to match where SPEC_impl.md states it (it is not edited in the archive). TODO.md's
  `Near term` bucket gains an entry: deliver recipe credentials through the agent's launch environment instead of its
  settings files (Claude `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; Codex provider via
  `-c` overrides with an `env_key` token; Codex Subscription stays in `auth.json`), noting the costs raised in triage
  (only Farhelm-started shells get the credentials, rotation reaches agents at next launch, a one-time cleanup of keys
  earlier releases wrote, spec rewrite) and that it would remove this race. No code change. Remove the feedback file and
  its index entry, and move this entry to `TRIAGE_OUTCOMES_ARCHIVE.md` in the same change.
- Execution: change `kssuvkxopmmyqspynukkvvrznvlkmvrr`, bookmark `docs/spec-settings-save-gap`,
  [PR #3293](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/3293/changes).

## sticky-parent-guard-contradicts-own-docs.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main e9ea6d08 (not run), by a delegated checker whose verdict triage
  reviewed. Claim: the recorder's and deflake's parent-directory checks accept any sticky parent, which contradicts
  their docs' promise to refuse a `/tmp/farhelm-tmp` that another account created first. Current main confirms it.
  `scripts/record-test-run.py:304` returns `st_uid in (euid, 0) or S_ISVTX`. Its docstring (296-300) says that in a
  sticky directory "only an entry's owner may rename or remove it", and names exactly the case where "another account
  could create `/tmp/farhelm-tmp` first". `deflake/bin/deflake:110` has the same check, and its docstring (96-102)
  promises refusal of "a `farhelm-tmp` it owns". `docs/test-run-evidence.md:120-121` says "otherwise another account
  that created the fixed-name directory first could swap or read the evidence." On Linux, the owner of a sticky
  directory can rename or unlink any entry in it. A sticky directory owned by this user or by root already passes the
  uid test, so the sticky clause only ever admits a sticky directory owned by another account, which is the case the
  docs promise to refuse. `scripts/test-record-test-run.py:1768-1793` asserts that acceptance (a stranger-owned 1777
  parent is safe) and repeats the wrong rationale in its docstring. SPEC_impl.md:5295-5297 ("Development tooling assumes
  a single-user machine… need not defend against one") keeps this out of `highest`. It does not make the docs' claim
  true.
- Decision: recorded without a per-item question on the maintainer's 2026-10-26 instruction to auto-triage every
  remaining item that is not likely mooted by the planned infallible GUI–helm connection (TODO.md), is clearly a bug
  needing no spec or product judgment, and is straightforward to fix without complexity or scope creep. The user can
  revise it.
- Completion criteria: in `safe_parent` (`scripts/record-test-run.py`) and `prepare_state_root` (`deflake/bin/deflake`),
  accept the parent only when this user or root owns it, dropping the sticky alternative; root-owned `/tmp` still
  passes. Fix both docstrings' sticky rationale. In `docs/test-run-evidence.md:120-121`, replace "or be sticky like
  `/tmp`" with the owner-or-root rule. Change `test_roots_owned_by_another_user_are_refused` in
  `scripts/test-record-test-run.py` to assert that a stranger-owned sticky parent is refused while a root-owned parent
  passes, and correct its docstring. Add the matching refusal case to `deflake/test-deflake.py` if it covers
  `prepare_state_root`. (If the maintainer prefers a docs-only correction that cites the SPEC_impl single-user rule, the

  reviewed. `FolderProblem::recognize` (crates/farhelm-ui/src/list/create_form.rs:1354-1366) checks the three supervisor
  phrases in a fixed order (Missing first) with `contains` over the whole refusal. The supervisor appends the literal
  cwd after its phrase (crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core.rs:3551, 3556, 3574). A not-a-directory refusal for a

  says "This folder does not exist on <host>" for an existing file. The type's own docs say the marking "only points at
  the field the refusal is about", which means the classification must follow the supervisor's actual phrase, not text
  inside the path. The marking authorizes nothing, so the impact is an advisory annotation only.

## neighbor-status-redraw-cancels-stable-url-click.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: already fixed. The desktop app still lets you click links in the terminal. A release counts as a click
  when the link found again under the pointer equals the pressed one

  numbers (`crates/gui/farhelm-grid-model/src/links.rs:313,376`), not per-row content identities. Redrawing an unrelated

## older-pin-success-clears-newer-stop-error.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: already fixed. The desktop app's operation store admits one request per session key at a time
  (`crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/operations.rs:15-21`, `Operations::start` → `admit` at :842-849). Pin goes through
  `menu::send` on `OpKey::session(key)` (`session_list/pins.rs:385-387`, `menu.rs:713-738`), so it is refused while that
  session's Stop is in flight, and a bulk Stop holds its keys too. A recorded refusal stays until the next operation on
  that key starts. A Pin can therefore only clear a Stop failure if the user starts it after that failure appears, which
  is not the overlapping route this finding describes. Checked by a delegated reader against main 28f177284 (code
  reading, not run); triage spot-checked the verdicts on high-bucket items.
- Decision: recorded without asking under the already-fixed rule (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/triage.md`, "Preparing
  each item").
- Completion criteria: remove the feedback file and its index entry; no code or spec change.
- Execution: `complete`; removed during the 2026-11-21 triage of findings that cited removed UI code.

## primary-row-drag-continues-through-middle-button.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: already fixed. The desktop app's drag watch ends on a left-button release only and ignores other buttons'
  releases (`crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/session_list/pin_drag.rs:960-961`). A move with the left button no longer held
  cancels the drag (:944-957: `held = event.pressed_button == Some(MouseButton::Left)`, otherwise `cancel_pin_drag`).
  Releasing the primary button mid-chord therefore ends the drag, and a later middle-button release can't commit a move.

## queued-recipe-edits-after-save-unresolved.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: already fixed. The desktop recipe editor locks the form synchronously when Save starts. `started` calls
  `set_saving(true)`, which marks every text input read-only on its own state
  (`crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/settings/recipes/editor.rs:476-491,580-586`), so later keystrokes are refused by the
  input regardless of repaint timing. The structural edits (choose software, add or remove a tunnel) return early while
  busy (:593-620). GPUI handles events one at a time on one thread, so no edit can slip in between capturing the draft
  and applying the lock. Checked by a delegated reader against main 28f177284 (code reading, not run); triage
  spot-checked the verdicts on high-bucket items.
- Decision: recorded without asking under the already-fixed rule (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/triage.md`, "Preparing

## repository-search-reports-empty-before-reply.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main e9ea6d08 (not run), by a delegated checker whose verdict triage
  reviewed. Claim: a partial repository query says "no repository matches" before the host has answered. Current main
  confirms it. `crates/farhelm-ui/src/list/create_form.rs:4129-4144` debounces 150 ms and then awaits
  `fetch_github_repositories`. While that is pending, `repository_result` is `None` and the suggestions are empty.
  `create_form.rs:4254-4259` builds the field's message by calling
  `empty_search_message(&format!("gh:{repository_text}"), false, false, false)`.
  `crates/farhelm-ui/src/launch_composer.rs:948` returns "no repository matches; enter owner/repo" unconditionally for a
  nonempty `gh:` value, and `create_form.rs:7001` shows that message whenever the list is empty. The `gh:` search scope
  (`create_form.rs:4266-4276`) also gets no repository-loading flag. The helper's own contract
  (`launch_composer.rs:917-922`, "Loading flags mean a read is still pending, not that a completed read failed") already
  handles pending reads this way for models ("loading models…") and templates ("loading templates…"). Repository
  discovery is the one pending source with no flag. SPEC.md:3228-3233 accepts that a repository search can be slow, but
  it does not accept a negative answer shown before the search finishes.
- Decision: recorded without a per-item question on the maintainer's 2026-10-26 instruction to auto-triage every
  remaining item that is not likely mooted by the planned infallible GUI–helm connection (TODO.md), is clearly a bug
  needing no spec or product judgment, and is straightforward to fix without complexity or scope creep. The user can
  revise it.
- Completion criteria: give `empty_search_message` a repository-loading input. Make its `SearchScope::Github` branch,
  for a nonempty value, return a loading message (wording parallel to "loading models…") while discovery for that entry
  point's current query is pending, which covers both the debounce and the wait for the host. Keep "no repository
  matches; enter owner/repo" for a completed reply for that query with no rows. Pass the flag from both callers in
  `create_form.rs`: the dedicated repository field, and the `gh:` search scope's `search_message`. In each, compute it
  as: a live repository authority whose query is this entry point's query, with no accepted result yet. Errors keep
  their existing note. Extend `empty_search_messages_cover_labels_and_loading` in `launch_composer.rs` with the
  repository-loading case, and with a case showing that the negative message still appears when not loading. Size gate:
  about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment);
  over it, block and bring it back. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: change `nqmwowtusqlmvstxuzyuyumssoxtyqoq`, bookmark
  `plan/launcher-repository-search-loading/01-repository-search-loading`,
  [PR #4388](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4388/changes).

## shutdown-wait-test-does-not-witness-waiting.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: confirmed by code reading on main e9ea6d08 (not run), by a delegated checker whose verdict triage
  reviewed. `the_stop_wait_is_bounded_and_covers_launches_still_starting`
  (crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core.rs:~27112-27166) has a stated purpose in its inline comment: "the wait
  must not end while it is in flight, and must pick it up once it registers". It takes a `starting_launch()` guard,
  spawns a task that sleeps 200ms, writes the mark, calls `track_pending_hold`, then drops the guard. It then only
  asserts that `wait_for_pending_holds` returns true. A broken wait that ignored `starting_launches` would find nothing
  pending and return true at once, so the test would still pass. The function's own doc (core.rs:~7003) promises: "the
  wait does not end while any are in flight".
- Decision: recorded without a per-item question on the maintainer's 2026-10-26 instruction to auto-triage every
  remaining item that is not likely mooted by the planned infallible GUI–helm connection (TODO.md), is clearly a bug
  needing no spec or product judgment, and is straightforward to fix without complexity or scope creep. The user can
  revise it.
- Completion criteria: Make the test fail if the wait returns before the in-flight launch registers. For example, have
  the registration task set a shared flag (e.g. an `Arc<AtomicBool>`) after `track_pending_hold` and before
  `drop(starting)`, and assert the flag is set as soon as `wait_for_pending_holds` returns, before joining the task. Do
  not rely on `JoinHandle::is_finished`, which can race the task's final poll. Update the test's comment to say what
  witnesses the wait. Optional confirmation: make the wait ignore `starting_launches` and check that the test now fails.
  Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog
  fragment); over it, block and bring it back. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: change `ksstuwwnvrlykrvnmnxuvtzruwkuktmx`, bookmark
  `plan/stop-wait-starting-launch-witness/01-starting-launch-witness`,
  [PR #4391](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4391/changes).

## block-copy-omits-wide-continuation-column.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: confirmed by a delegated reader against main 28f177284 (code reading, not run): A block (Alt-drag) copy
  takes the same columns on every row through `GridRow::text(from, to)`
  (`crates/gui/farhelm-grid-model/src/selection.rs:325-340`). When `from` falls on a wide character's second cell,
  `text` drops the character and emits no blank for that cell (`crates/gui/farhelm-grid-model/src/lib.rs:117-149`,
  "Starting on its spacer cell omits it"). That row's copied text is then one column shorter on the left than the other
  rows. The module still says the rules derive from xterm (`selection.rs:3-4`), and xterm emits a blank there.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "Not required; state it once" (2026-11-21 six-question triage page for findings that

  ported the same guess. `pads_wide_wrap` (`crates/gui/farhelm-grid-model/src/selection.rs:357-371`) treats a wrapped

## frozen-sandbox-retains-header-lifecycle-answers.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: confirmed by a delegated reader against main 28f177284 (code reading, not run): The header's Stop, Restart
  and Replace buttons are disabled while the environment is frozen
  (`crates/gui/farhelm-gui/src/session_pane/header.rs:1133-1189`), and the frozen check is applied when a question opens
  (`allows_active` at 795-799, `session_list/menu.rs:659-666`). Two paths miss it: - **Open header question.** A
  question that is already open stays open when the sandbox is suspended elsewhere: layers close only when their subject
  is gone (`layers.rs:498-504`). Its Confirm runs `restart::confirm` / `replace::confirm`
  (`session_list/restart.rs:248-250`, `session_list/replace.rs:270-279`) with no new frozen check. -
  **Interrupted-session card.** Its Replace button is disabled only by `menu::refused`
  (`session_pane/card.rs:427,506-523`). `replace_from_card` (about 614-640) checks only that the card still shows, not
  frozen state, so it asks and sends. The card's Restart click does check frozen (597-601), but the button is drawn
  enabled. In both cases the helm refuses because the host is not connected.
- Decision: the maintainer picked "Acceptable, and say so in the spec" for controls that stay answerable after their
  target changed when nothing harmful follows (2026-11-21 six-question triage page for findings that cited removed UI
  code, Q2). This entry carries the spec change for the group of five.
- Completion criteria: SPEC.md's GUI concurrency text (beside the 2026-10-26 convenience-state principle) states the
  principle: a control the screen still shows after its target changed may be used, as long as the helm refuses what is
  no longer valid or the result is trivially undone. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: change `svvztnrotlwpwlqxupmplvylqpkmszpt`, bookmark `pr/spec-stale-control-principle`,
  [PR #4394](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4394/changes).

## desktop-path-probe-needs-private-result-boundary.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: login_path.rs `NamedTempFile::new()` (TMPDIR), and the shell appends by path
  (`>> "$FARHELM_LOGIN_PATH_FILE"`). The default /tmp is sticky. Basis: SPEC.md "Local authority and trust between
  hosts": "Conditions the user, or whoever administers their machine, deliberately set up outside Farhelm count as the
  user's intent: their shell environment ... If the trigger takes a deliberate setup and the consequence follows from
  what that setup means, guarding against it is not Farhelm's job." Because the item is highest, the coordinator may
  want an independent check before removing it.
- Decision: recorded without asking (fewest-questions triage, 2026-11-21, against main ca62397de). The finding's
  possible harm could be in the `highest` bucket, so the drop went through the independent drop check
  (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/recording.md`, "Independent drop check"), which agreed: narrowly: needs TMPDIR
  deliberately pointed at a non-sticky directory other accounts can write (SPEC.md deliberate setup); the app reads back
  through its own handle, so no PATH injection.
- Completion criteria: remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: complete (removed during triage).

## terminal-file-requests-can-wait-indefinitely.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: covered. No admission deadline exists, which SPEC_impl states explicitly ("There is no upload staging,
  publication phase, admission cap or progress timer"). A healthy supervisor answers; a stall needs a hung filesystem, a
  slow host, or a broken host. The rest of Farhelm keeps working, and leaving the view ends the wait. Basis: SPEC.md
  "Healthy local filesystems" ("Requests involving the affected host may fail or remain pending, but the helm must
  otherwise continue to function"), "Slow hosts", and the 2026-10-11 denial-of-service acceptance for arbitrarily broken
  hosts. Caveat: SPEC_impl's "every host-waiting route the GUI sends is bounded" phrase could be read against this. If

- Assessment: The code is unchanged. `harness.rs` `grid_text` adds a newline after every row. `codex_identity.rs`
  `complete_marker` and `harness.rs` `extract_pid` trust that newline, and `session_lifecycle.rs` ~L4002 kills the
  parsed `self_pid`. The route needs one short `writeln!`/`println!` to be split mid-line on the pty, and that is not
  established. Std's LineWriter flushes the buffered "SELF-PID:<digits>" in a single write before the newline, so a
  split inside the digits is very unlikely. Basis: "Harm whose route is not established in shipped code". Every
  consequence depends on an unshown mid-write split. The killing of an unrelated process is a highest-class consequence,
  so FILTER.md requires the independent drop check before dropping, even though the bucket is other.
- Decision: recorded without asking (fewest-questions triage, 2026-11-21, against main ca62397de). The finding's
  possible harm could be in the `highest` bucket, so the drop went through the independent drop check
  (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/recording.md`, "Independent drop check"), which agreed: both the false test failure
  and the kill need the SELF-PID line split inside its digits, which the single buffered writeln does not produce;
  maintainer tests only.
- Completion criteria: remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: complete (removed during triage).

## macos-shift-sweep-can-miss-release.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: On macOS, pressing Control just before releasing a Shift sweep can make Farhelm miss the release; at the
  list edge it keeps scrolling and changing marks until the next mouse move, which then cancels the sweep and restores
  the earlier marks. Verified: the release listener only accepts `MouseButton::Left` (`pin_drag.rs:959-962`); the next
  move without a held Left cancels (`:943-956`). Vendor modifier mapping not re-read. Rare input combination; visible
  and reversible.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Discarded as decided. Change `mwnyupmuwnrp`, bookmark `plan/triage-bookkeeping/01-discards`,
  [PR #4465](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4465/changes).

## repeated-resizes-clear-missing-history-notice.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: After a recovery from a checkpoint too large to keep all scrollback (over 16 MiB), resizing the terminal
  taller and shorter repeatedly can make the "earlier output could not be recovered" notice disappear early. Verified:
  emulator.rs `trim_remaining` subtracts the monotonic `lines_scrolled_into_history`, which resize re-entry also
  increments (vendor behavior per the file; vendor not re-read). SPEC.md:3263 says the notice "stays until the program
  clears its scrollback or the scrollback has turned over". The fix needs resize accounting, not one obvious line.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Discarded as decided. Change `mwnyupmuwnrp`, bookmark `plan/triage-bookkeeping/01-discards`,
  [PR #4465](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4465/changes).

## empty-history-clear-keeps-missing-history-notice.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: If a recovered checkpoint had to drop all of its scrollback, a program's clear-scrollback (`CSI 3 J`) does
  not dismiss the "earlier output could not be recovered" notice. Verified: emulator.rs ends the mark only on a
  `history_clears` change. The file says the vendor `clear_history` is skipped when history is empty (not re-read).
  SPEC.md:3263 promises the notice ends when the program clears scrollback. The fix has several possible shapes (a
  vendor patch, or a hook in the query wrapper), so it is not SETTLED.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main

## reconnect-replay-keeps-obsolete-event-count-fence.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: In a rare reconnect during a supervisor's initial terminal restore, a session can stay marked "still
  restoring". Agent-to-agent prompts to it are refused and its status is not sampled until the program prints anything
  more, such as the user typing. Verified: The prompt refusal is at core.rs:12045-12051 (`caught_up`). The event-count
  fence persisting across reconnect is taken from the file's citations. The trigger needs EventQueueFull during a resize
  in the restore window. It heals on new output, but not unaided while the program is idle, so it does not fully match
  the rare self-correcting filter.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Discarded as decided. Change `mwnyupmuwnrp`, bookmark `plan/triage-bookkeeping/01-discards`,
  [PR #4465](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4465/changes).

## mixed-input-acknowledgements-misattribute-written-bytes.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: After a rare kernel allocation failure on a terminal write, one dropped keystroke batch can be reported
  internally as written when a later batch succeeds before the acknowledgement is sent. Nothing user-visible depends on
  it today: the agent-prompt consumer that waits on this result is disabled in production. Verified: `hosts/terminal.rs`
  `acknowledge` still assigns written bytes first, in order, and its docstring states the approximation. The
  terminal-host protocol (crates/terminal-host/SPEC.md, "Input") sends cumulative totals that cannot express a discard
  followed by a write within one acknowledgement. An exact fix therefore needs a host-side or protocol change, and
  running hosts outlive releases. The ENOMEM trigger was not reproduced.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Discarded as decided. Change `mwnyupmuwnrp`, bookmark `plan/triage-bookkeeping/01-discards`,
  [PR #4465](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4465/changes).

## snapshot-state-races-build-admission.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: Confirming a new sandbox host just as that recipe's build finishes can pick a snapshot that was just
  retired (setup fails) or start an unneeded charged build. A Rebuild during the add can also retire the chosen snapshot
  before the host is created. Verified: Still present. `tensorlake/build.rs` `ensure_snapshot` reads state before
  checking `is_building`. The finish-between-reads case is a millisecond window. The rebuild-during-add case needs the
  user's own concurrent Rebuild. The outcome is a failed setup (retry works) or an extra build.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Discarded as decided. Change `mwnyupmuwnrp`, bookmark `plan/triage-bookkeeping/01-discards`,
  [PR #4465](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4465/changes).

  cannot find `sleep`. Verified: Confirmed that the relaunch helper runs `sleep 0.1` by name (updater.rs ~343, bundle.rs

## linux-second-launch-lost-during-quit.md

- Outcome: `discard`.
- Assessment: On Linux, reopening Farhelm while the old window is quitting can end with no window: the new launch hands
  off to the quitting one and exits. Verified: `forward_to_running`
  (`crates/farhelm-desktop/src/second_launch.rs:45-52`) counts a successful connect as the handoff. `retire` removes the
  socket at quit, and its comment acknowledges the window that remains before that. The window is narrow. Relaunching
  again works.
- Decision: Q10, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (discard). (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.

## guarded-delete-replace-omits-surviving-shell-work.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: After a shell session's main shell exits, background jobs it left in the session can keep running. Delete
  or Replace then shows "nothing is running" (or asks nothing) or names only tabs, and still kills those jobs. Agent
  approval cards for Delete do the same. Verified: SPEC.md lifecycle (~2147): "An agent exiting on its own does not
  trigger a hunt for daemonized survivors; the session's next restart or its teardown does." The refusal rule names only
  "the agent or any terminal tab". Teardown sweeps the whole session. I did not re-trace the supervisor guard line by
  line.
- Decision: Q3, the maintainer picked "Hang up shells; accept the reaping". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page
  (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of
  plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Add to SPEC: a Stop, Delete or Replace prompt for a session whose main program has ended covers
  its leftover background jobs, and teardown reaps them. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: `rmrmvworuyoorsnuussorptztnyxqppn`, `plan/triage-spec-text/01-accepted-behavior`,
  [draft PR](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4467/changes). Fixed as decided.

## automatic-update-planning-serializes-hosts.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: With automatic host updates on, the helm plans each host's update one at a time, so a slow host (slow SSH,
  or a held environment-delete lock of up to 240 s) delays when later hosts' automatic updates begin. Nothing
  interactive waits; only the background start order is delayed. Verified: automatic.rs `scan` loops over hosts and
  awaits `plan_update` + `start_automatic_update` per host serially (confirmed). Each wait is bounded. The 240 s second
  wait was not re-traced. SPEC.md "Waiting between operations on one host" says "other hosts" must not wait on slow
  work; "Slow hosts" says one slow host "must not stop the helm serving the others". Neither says whether background
  automatic-update scheduling counts.
- Decision: Q9, the maintainer picked "Approve as listed" (write the current behavior into the spec). (2026-11-21
  fewest-questions triage page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these
  in a much smaller set of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running
  concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Apply the recommendation with no code change: Allow it. Fix spec with one sentence saying
  background automatic-update starts may be serialized with bounded waits as long as interactive service to other hosts
  is unaffected. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: `rmrmvworuyoorsnuussorptztnyxqppn`, `plan/triage-spec-text/01-accepted-behavior`,
  [draft PR](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4467/changes). Fixed as decided.

## macos-terminal-paste-blocks-gui-thread.md

- Outcome: `fix spec`.
- Assessment: Pasting into a terminal on macOS reads the clipboard on the window's main thread. When the clipboard is
  slow to deliver its contents (for example Universal Clipboard pulling text copied on an iPhone, or a hung app that
  owns the clipboard), the whole Farhelm window freezes until it arrives. Verified: Confirmed.
  `vendor/gpui-pre-macos/src/platform.rs` `read_from_clipboard_async` returns `Task::ready(read_payload())`. Its comment
  says this is deliberate, to keep AppKit's thread ownership, and admits the read still blocks. SPEC.md ~3406-3408: "A
  broken, hung or slow clipboard ... nothing else in Farhelm may stall because of it." The code contradicts that, but
  the choice was deliberate, so this is not SETTLED.
- Decision: Q5, the maintainer picked "Allow a requested paste to wait". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: SPEC: a paste the user asked for may wait on a slow macOS clipboard; everything else keeps the
  no-stall rule. No code change. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: `rmrmvworuyoorsnuussorptztnyxqppn`, `plan/triage-spec-text/01-accepted-behavior`,
  [draft PR](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4467/changes). Fixed as decided.

## bulk-mute-can-reset-window.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: With more than about 65 sessions marked, choosing Mute or Unmute (and probably Pin or Mark read too) sends
  one command per row in a single burst. The helm closes the connection once more than 64 are waiting, so the window
  goes through "Reconnecting to the helm…" with only part of the batch applied. Verified: Confirmed.
  `session_list/marking.rs` ~897-922 sends every eligible write at once. `ui_channel.rs` `MAX_QUEUED_COMMANDS = 64`
  closes the channel when exceeded, with the comment "A real GUI never comes close", which bulk marking makes false.
  SPEC.md ~2347-2349 says metadata choices "reuse the ordinary writes", and SPEC.md "Losing the connection to the helm"
  expects resets only on real connection failure. Not measured: how fast the helm drains the queue.
- Decision: Q8 (fix the code), the maintainer wrote: "approve as listed for any where the fix is straight forward and
  does not involve significant additional complexity. For any where that is not true, please come back to me in the next
  update on this page." This item was judged straightforward. (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page (main
  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Apply the recommendation: Fix code. Pace bulk metadata writes the way bulk Stop/Delete already
  are. If the fix turns out not to be straightforward, or needs significant additional complexity, stop and bring it
  back to the maintainer. Size gate: about 100 lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue

## sidebar-order-stays-held-after-shift-sweep.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.

  if the pointer stays still. Verified: `pin_drag_moved` calls `pointer_activity` for every captured move wherever the
  pointer is (`pin_drag.rs:1171-1177`), which sets `pointer_over = true` (`hold.rs:138-143`); the capture stops the
  rows' own hover listener, so no leave arrives until the next move. SPEC.md: the client shows the order again "as soon
  as the pointer leaves the list", and "an active marking sweep keeps the hold even if the pointer leaves". Ending the
  hold at sweep end is implied, not written, so not clearly settled.

  ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of plans.
  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Apply the recommendation: fix code (only count captured moves inside the rows' bounds as

## working-attention-row-hides-warning-edge.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: session_list/attention.rs ~253 sets `warning: kind == Kind::Problem && status.warned`, so a Working row
  (live progress) never carries the edge. hosts/status.rs `follow` keeps the warning latched during a Running retry and
  clears it only on Completed or when Hosts opens. The cue bookkeeping (~395-419) drops the reason while the row is
  Working, so the cue can replay when work ends. Basis: SPEC.md "Hosts needing attention" (~2868): "An attention row
  keeps an amber left edge while SSH needs an answer or retry, a setup or update failure needs attention, or a host has
  an identity or ownership problem." The same section makes live progress take precedence for the row's content only.
  Fix: set `warning` from `status.warned` for Working rows too (and SignIn rows, if wanted). Keeping the reason present
  also stops the cue from replaying. Caveat for the coordinator: this reads "needs attention" as including a failure
  whose retry is running. That fits the latch in status.rs, but demote to DECIDE if that reading is in doubt.
- Decision: recorded under the clearly-settled rule (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/triage.md`, "Preparing each item")
  without asking (fewest-questions triage, 2026-11-21, against main ca62397de). The maintainer can revise it.
- Completion criteria: fix the code so it matches the quoted rule, with a test where practical. Size gate: about 100
  lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment); over that,
  execution blocks and brings the item back to the maintainer. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Fixed. A host retry keeps the amber warning beside its live progress until the warning clears. jj change
  `votqulzktmpz`, bookmark `plan/triage-gui-sessions/02-attention-and-upload-notices`,
  [draft PR #4477](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4477/changes).

## suspend-treats-failed-session-refresh-as-complete.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: session_list/environment.rs `activity_asks` (~503-518) checks only `HostStateView::Connected { .. }`, not
  truncation or staleness, and ignores the host's `refresh: RefreshView::Failed`. `GET /api/sessions` serves the helm's
  retained cache. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows and leaves the host Connected (ui_channel.rs ~1152-1162).
  Basis: SPEC.md "Topology" ~352-354: "Suspend asks first when an agent on that host is working, its status is unknown
  or stale, or activity cannot be checked completely. Immediate Suspend requires a connected host after the activity
  read and a complete listing with conclusive non-working statuses." A failed refresh means activity was not checked.
  Fix: ask unless the host's refresh view is Ok.
- Decision: recorded under the clearly-settled rule (`review_feedback_queue/.agents/triage.md`, "Preparing each item")
  without asking (fewest-questions triage, 2026-11-21, against main ca62397de). The maintainer can revise it.
- Completion criteria: fix the code so it matches the quoted rule, with a test where practical. Size gate: about 100
  lines of diff (code, tests and docs, not counting this ledger, the queue removal or a changelog fragment); over that,
  execution blocks and brings the item back to the maintainer. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: Fixed. A connected host needs a successful session refresh before Suspend can skip the activity
  confirmation. jj change `ktwlysusrtrp`, bookmark `plan/triage-gui-sessions/03-environment-cards-and-questions`,
  [draft PR #4481](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4481/changes).

## trailing-primary-write-notice-filter-drag-guidance.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.

  of them running concurrently."

- Assessment: Maintainer workflow only. A delayed `queue answer` to an old plan question can be attached to that plan's
  newer question and send the plan back to pending. Verified: Still true. plans-queue.py `answer` checks only that the
  plan is blocked (~1063-1076), and landing.md ~207-208 claims "Exit 10 means someone else answered or changed the plan
  first". No unauthorized protected action is established.
- Decision: Q14, the maintainer picked "Fix only what corrupts evidence or crashes". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage
  page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set
  of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Fix it if the bug crashes a documented command, loses or misattributes test or release evidence,
  turns a real verdict into a harness failure, or lets private data into a fixture; otherwise make no change. Either way
  remove the feedback file and its index entry, and say in the execution record which way it went. Recommendation for
  reference: Discard. Or a small fix: bind the answer to a hash of the question.
- Execution: No change under Q14. A stale answer can advance the wrong blocked question. The review established a queue
  transition and left downstream authorization harm unverified. jj change `qxvpwulr`, bookmark
  `plan/triage-tooling/05-plans-workflow-items`, [draft PR #4499](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4499/changes).

## closed-conflicting-pr-does-not-wake-executor.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: Maintainer workflow only. An idle executor that skipped a plan because another plan's open PR conflicted
  with it does not wake when that PR is closed without a queue change. Verified: Still true. The plans-queue.py wake
  docstring (~1259-1268) says "the filter cannot see PRs".
- Decision: Q14, the maintainer picked "Fix only what corrupts evidence or crashes". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage
  page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set
  of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Fix it if the bug crashes a documented command, loses or misattributes test or release evidence,
  turns a real verdict into a harness failure, or lets private data into a fixture; otherwise make no change. Either way
  remove the feedback file and its index entry, and say in the execution record which way it went. Recommendation for
  reference: Discard (a manual drain or any queue change recovers).
- Execution: No change under Q14. Closing a PR alone can leave eligible work idle until the executor rechecks the queue.
  jj change `qxvpwulr`, bookmark `plan/triage-tooling/05-plans-workflow-items`,
  [draft PR #4499](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4499/changes).

## stable-recut-removes-retained-announcement-anchor.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: If a stable release with an in-app announcement fails after its tag is pushed and is re-cut as the next
  patch version, the announcement's "Release notes" link points at a version anchor the website no longer has. The link
  opens the release-notes page but not the right section. Verified: Confirmed. `releasing/.agents/stable.md`,
  "Re-cutting a stable release", keeps each entry's version on purpose and renames the CHANGELOG heading.
  `release_announcements.rs` builds `#vX.Y.Z` from the entry's version. `website/scripts/release-notes.mjs` emits
  anchors only from CHANGELOG headings. The trigger is rare (stable announcement + spent tag + re-cut).
- Decision: Q14, the maintainer picked "Fix only what corrupts evidence or crashes". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage
  page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set
  of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Fix it if the bug crashes a documented command, loses or misattributes test or release evidence,
  turns a real verdict into a harness failure, or lets private data into a fixture; otherwise make no change. Either way
  remove the feedback file and its index entry, and say in the execution record which way it went. Recommendation for
  reference: discard. The link still reaches the page. If fixed, an alias anchor for the spent version is the smallest
  change.
- Execution: No change under Q14. The retained announcement still opens the release notes page, but its original version
  fragment can miss the renamed section after a re-cut. jj change `zrlsrywvqylx`, bookmark
  `plan/triage-tooling/06-release-and-brick-tooling`,
  [draft PR #4502](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4502/changes).

## brick-recovery-truncates-checkpoint-budget.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: None for users. In the Mac release brick test, a recoverable provider rate limit (429) can leave the slow
  old-session checks with too little time for their retry, or block the retry outright under a small `--timeout`.
  Verified: Confirmed. `brick_test.py` gives the first task `turn_timeout(...)` (2400/1800 s floors) but sets
  `checkpoint_deadline = clock + timeout` from the raw `--timeout`. BRICK-TEST.md contradicts itself: line ~395 says
  "`--timeout` bounds each checkpoint including backoff", while ~529 says these checkpoints get at least 2400/1800 s.
  Not covered by plan brick-test-guard-oracles (its acceptance is about other guards).
- Decision: Q14, the maintainer picked "Fix only what corrupts evidence or crashes". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage
  page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set
  of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Fix it if the bug crashes a documented command, loses or misattributes test or release evidence,
  turns a real verdict into a harness failure, or lets private data into a fixture; otherwise make no change. Either way
  remove the feedback file and its index entry, and say in the execution record which way it went. Recommendation for
  reference: fix code + doc. Base the deadline on the effective first-turn timeout and reconcile the two BRICK-TEST.md
  sentences.
- Execution: Fixed. Each checkpoint’s effective first-turn budget also bounds backoff and retries. A pre-action refusal
  on the 2400-second old fixture can retry with 2330 seconds left after ten seconds of elapsed time and a 60-second
  backoff. jj change `zrlsrywvqylx`, bookmark `plan/triage-tooling/06-release-and-brick-tooling`,
  [draft PR #4502](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4502/changes).

## trailing-selected-above-handoff-floor-legacy-target-missing-tmux-launch-advice.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: A Mac user who picks an older release (for example v0.35.0, above the handoff floor) through
  `FARHELM_VERSION` gets no tmux prerequisite advice from the current installer. That old app then refuses to start
  without tmux, with its own remedy alert. Verified: `scripts/install.sh` has no tmux handling, and
  `HANDOFF_FLOOR=0.31.1-dev.0` (:101). SPEC.md:5674-5675: "Farhelm neither requires nor looks for one on any machine."
  No spec text speaks to selected older targets.
- Decision: Q14, the maintainer picked "Fix only what corrupts evidence or crashes". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage
  page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set
  of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Fix it if the bug crashes a documented command, loses or misattributes test or release evidence,
  turns a real verdict into a harness failure, or lets private data into a fixture; otherwise make no change. Either way
  remove the feedback file and its index entry, and say in the execution record which way it went. Recommendation for
  reference: discard (explicit old-release selection is rare, and the old app gives its own actionable refusal)
- Execution: No change under Q14. The current installer gives no advance tmux advice for selected older releases. The
  older app itself reports its missing prerequisite and remedy. jj change `zrlsrywvqylx`, bookmark
  `plan/triage-tooling/06-release-and-brick-tooling`,
  [draft PR #4502](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4502/changes).

## brick-test-deferral-reuses-continuity-files.md

- Outcome: `other`.
- Assessment: Maintainer release tooling only. During the Mac release brick test, if the remote-update check defers or
  fails before taking its own counter sample, the harness can report a harness error instead of the real failure
  verdict. Verified: Code unchanged since be6cb86e1. `self.state` is pass-wide (`managed-state.json` in pass_dir).
  `save_record` exports `state['continuity']` for remote-update (guest_operations.py ~299). `continuity_remote_after`
  raises ObservationNotReady before sampling (~828), which leaves continuity-before's receipt names in place.
  guest_tester.py ~345 copies those names into the result, and `validate_observation` resolves them in the current
  attempt's directory (~471-480), where they do not exist, so it raises TesterError. Not covered by plan
  brick-test-guard-oracles. Real incidence is unmeasured.
- Decision: Q14, the maintainer picked "Fix only what corrupts evidence or crashes". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage
  page (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set
  of plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Fix it if the bug crashes a documented command, loses or misattributes test or release evidence,
  turns a real verdict into a harness failure, or lets private data into a fixture; otherwise make no change. Either way
  remove the feedback file and its index entry, and say in the execution record which way it went. Recommendation for
  reference: fix code (keep the exported continuity names attempt-local and add a test that defers after a real earlier
  pair)
- Execution: Fixed. Each attempt exports its own continuity filenames. A deferral after a prior checkpoint’s saved pair
  can preserve its unavailable verdict, and a completed sample still exports its two files. jj change `zrlsrywvqylx`,
  bookmark `plan/triage-tooling/06-release-and-brick-tooling`,
  [draft PR #4502](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4502/changes).

  place and recipe deletion clean up that place's owned images." Tensorlake's rebuild replaces only after success

  please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Apply the recommendation: Fix code: force the rebuild with a flag and retire the old images only

  queue removal or a changelog fragment); over that, execution blocks and brings the item back to the maintainer. Remove

  a good chance of them running concurrently."

  asks for an explicit confirmation and then settles the pending marker, so the recipe can be deleted and its container
  host removed or retargeted. Medium; the maintainer accepted the new confirmation path. Remove the feedback file and
  its index entry.

## retargeted-ssh-alias-can-forget-live-container.md

- Outcome: `fix spec+code`.
- Assessment: A container session's host is reached through an SSH alias. If the user repoints that alias in their SSH
  config to another machine or account, Delete checks the new machine, finds no container, reports success and drops the
  session from Hosts. The real container keeps running on the old machine with nothing in Farhelm managing it. Verified:
  Confirmed on main. `environment/podman.rs` `place()` compares only the registry route (destination string + config
  path). `destroy`/`remove_container` treat Podman's "absent" on that route as proof. No machine or account identity is
  recorded or checked for Podman places. SPEC.md ~322-326 has identity-change detection for ordinary host connections
  ("never silently merges"), and SPEC.md 5285-5296 treats deliberate setup outside Farhelm as the user's intent. Which
  of the two governs here is unsettled.
- Decision: Q4, the maintainer picked "Apply the ordinary identity rules". (2026-11-21 fewest-questions triage page
  (main ca62397de).) Maintainer's note on execution: "yes we definitely need to batch these in a much smaller set of
  plans. please try to separate them by area of code so there is a good chance of them running concurrently."
- Completion criteria: Container hosts reached over SSH follow the ordinary host identity rules: record the machine and
  account identity when a container is bound, refuse to accept "absent" as proof of deletion under a different identity,
  and refuse twin container hosts that reach the same machine and account. Update SPEC accordingly. Both identity items
  may land together. Remove the feedback file and its index entry.
- Execution: `tqutnrkvprvxxxtzqlupqrtupnyosmuy`, `plan/triage-podman/04-container-host-identity`,
  [draft PR](https://github.com/scode/farhelm/pull/4504/changes). Deferred to TODO.md, Near term → Plan follow-up,
  “Apply host identity rules to Podman places”. An absent container with no recorded original identity cannot
  distinguish a removed resource from a changed route.

## valid-ssh-uri-short-label-parsing.md

- Outcome: `fix code`.
- Assessment: host_name.rs `destination_host` strips a URI port only when `is_port` (non-empty, all digits) holds, so
  the suffix stays, `IpAddr` parsing fails and the address is cut at its first dot (confirmed). The trailing-slash form
  in the file's TLDR is not detailed and is unverified. Basis: SPEC.md:287-291, "Short name": "removes `ssh://`, a user
  prefix through the last `@`, brackets, and a port only in an SSH URI ... IP addresses stay whole". Code contradicts
  this for `:ssh` and empty ports. Direct fix: in URI mode, strip any colon-free suffix after the last `:`, including an
  empty one. Caveat for the coordinator: whether a service name counts as a "port" is mildly reading-dependent;
  downgrade to DECIDE (same question as the abbreviated-IPv4 item) if you want strictness.

  without asking (fewest-questions triage, 2026-11-21, against main ca62397de). The maintainer can revise it.
